Following `math_gate` **literally would not have worked**:
`lower_constraint_violation_rules` only matches a consequent bound to one of the two
`math:` ℚ⁷ dimension builtins, and no kernel law has one. Applied to `logic/module.ttl` it
lowers **0 of 45** constraints — the gate would have stayed exactly as dead, with more code
in front of it. The lowering was extended in the canonical lane instead.

### The law census

| | count |
|---|---|
| Authored `logic:Constraint`s in `slices/grounding/logic/module.ttl` | **45** |
| Lower into violation rules | **25** → 56 rules (one per consequent conjunct) |
| Decline | **20** |
| **Enactment-kernel laws among the 25** | **23 of 23** |

All 20 declines are `no-enforces-failure-class` — **none** declines for want of
expressiveness. They are 7 `gmeow:` advice/term-completeness laws and 13 `logic:` IR-shape
/ teleology laws whose enforcement surface is the derived SHACL that `make validate` runs.
`reject_unenforced_laws` hard-fails if a law that *does* carry
`gmeow:enforcesFailureClass` fails to lower, so the residue cannot silently grow.

**Every kernel law this issue authored is now reasoner-enforced.**

### How the laws compile

`∀x. guard(x) → consequent`, one violation rule **per consequent conjunct**, negating that
conjunct: an obligation `p(x,?y)` → NAF literal `¬p(x,?y)`; a prohibition `¬p(x,y)` →
positive literal. Per-conjunct matters — a single rule carrying `¬ψ₁ ∧ ¬ψ₂` fires only when
*both* legs break, silently passing a record that omits one mandatory field.

No `rdfs:seeAlso` map, and that was reasoned rather than cargo-culted: `math_gate` needs one
because its laws predicate over HiLog reflection relations no data asserts; the kernel's
ASTs name object-level properties directly. A blanket map would have silently rewritten any
predicate carrying an `rdfs:seeAlso` for an unrelated documentary reason.

Required one piece of ontology work: the 23 kernel laws carried no failure class, so there
was nothing to mark a violation with (the lowering never fabricates one). Added
`logic:EnactmentIntegrityViolation`, mirroring the shape `math:DimensionalInhomogeneity`
already has over its two laws.

## Stage 2 · Gap G5 — CRITICAL — the CLI printed the author's frontier label as DERIVED (fixed)

**Commit:** `beda510ed`

The subcommand printed a column headed `DERIVED LABEL`, appended `(derived)`, and read
`logic:entryLabel` from the union of the asserted EDB and the derived quads **with no
provenance split**. Its own help promised *"a stale hand-written label shows up as a
disagreement rather than being echoed back"*. It did not: a label contradicting its own axis
witness was echoed under `DERIVED LABEL` with no flag, and `--why-not` stamped `(derived)`

### The subtle half — why the obvious fix was not enough

Carrying the reasoner's existing EDB/IDB split through (`ASSERT_RULE_IRI` vs the firing
rule's IRI) was step one. But **the reasoner works over sets**: an asserted label that a
rule *would also* conclude is already present, so nothing re-emits it — an author who was
exactly right would have been reported as unverified.

So the frontier path now runs a second **audit materialization** over the same input with
every asserted `logic:entryLabel` withheld, taking only that run's conclusions as the
derived set. `logic:entryLabel` is a head in all 16 shipped rules and appears in no body, so
withholding it cannot subtract anything else. Cost ~0.15s. That is what makes "still
re-derived" literally true rather than approximately true.

#### The finding now names the law — and that turned out to be load-bearing

All 40 laws deliberately share one `gmeow:enforcesFailureClass`, so every violation rule was
headed on the **same tuple shape** `?record rdf:type logic:EnactmentIntegrityViolation`. The
chase materializes a *set* and keeps one winning derivation per tuple — so **a record

only in the derivation provenance, which does not survive into the tuple.

record also breaks a presence law, which won the tuple and masked it. **Any real corpus
record breaking two kernel laws was under-reported the same way** — this was not a test

distinct tuples and neither can displace the other. `reject_colliding_heads` hard-fails if
two constraints ever emit the same head shape again.

An earlier diagnosis of mine blamed body-literal ordering breaking NAF safety. It was
**refuted empirically** — forcing every negated literal last changes nothing, because both
evaluators partition the body and apply negation after the complete positive join. Recorded
in the commit so it is not re-investigated.

**All 15 relational laws are now verified to fire on the relational failure they name**, each
through the real `verify()` path. The guard test that stayed green throughout this bug now

a reader that walks `quads()` alone never sees an attributed statement at all. Two boundaries
became honest instead of silent: a quad in a **named graph** hard-fails (merging distinct
worlds lets a fact in one satisfy a rule body about another), and a triple-term-bearing fact is
carried into the row set but **withheld from the reasoning world and reported** — the engine's
term codec has no triple-term surface and feeding one in returns a malformed IRI. Reporting
beats mangling.

```
BEFORE  proposalRequiredContract: Page image in, positioned text out.   <- @en stripped
        proposalExpectedInputs: 300                                     <- datatype stripped
AFTER   "Page image in, positioned text out."@en
        "300"^^<http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#nonNegativeInteger>
        + warning …statement-metadata-not-reasoned: carries 1 RDF 1.2 statement-metadata fact(s)
```

**G16 — the derived frontier was a dead end.** All four `logic` subcommands now take
`--format text|json`, reusing the flag `logic fragments` already had rather than inventing a
second convention. Every document carries the full derived closure with the provenance split,
the witnesses and the outcome. `explain` always emits all five elements as keys, empty when
unrecorded, **so dissent cannot vanish by omission**.

**G17 — zero RDF 1.2 statement metadata in the examples.** Three uses, six reifiers, each
expressing something a plain triple cannot: two co-equal vantages taking opposite stances on
one preference *statement*; a reconciliation verdict attributed to the **provider whose word
licenses the retry** rather than to the record; and the same verdict claimed by one instrument
and withheld by another, which otherwise needs a second `ReconciliationResult` and reads as two
reconciliations for one probe. Two reifiers wherever the vantages are co-equal.

**G18 — the shape-scan exemption was a blanket.** Any hand-authored shape parked in *any*
slice's `counter-examples/` was invisible to the projection-purity gate. The exemption is now
keyed on **actual registration**, read per slice. Demonstrated: an unregistered shape smuggled
into that directory took the scan from `scanned 0 … exit=0` to `[NO-PROJECTED-PEER] … exit=1`.

**G21 — `RETIRED_SLICES` was safe but unpinned.** The retired slice genuinely no longer exists,
but nothing prevented a **live** slice being added, and the floors gate simply `continue`d with
no count check. Both files now assert no entry names a slice that still exists, reading
liveness from the same discovery the sweep and carrier use, refusing to pass vacuously.
Teeth proved by temporarily adding a live slice and watching it panic.

**Also fixed (found in passing, not on the known-red list):** conformance's `run.rs` used
`Result<_, String>`, violating the Diag-substrate invariant and redding `repo_static`. It came
in with my own conformance-corpus commit.

`gmeow-cli` 129 · `dev_shapes` 32 · `gmeow-conformance` 854 · gmn1 gate 10 · `example_sweep` 7,
allowlist still 35 · clippy and fmt clean.

## Stage 2 · Gap G19 — HIGH — the doc-coverage debt this branch created (paid)

**Commit:** `269790cb9`

A comment on this branch claimed *"No axis rose"*. That was true only against the branch's own
earlier peak; **against `origin/main` nine axes had risen**.

Measured properly first: main has **6507** terms, the branch **6842** — 384 minted, 49 removed
with the retired slice. Every one of the 384 now carries a `skos:scopeNote` that says something
the definition does not (the boundary, the sibling it is confused with, or what it deliberately
does **not** assert), and the 155 that lacked them gained `useWhen`, `avoidWhen`, `howToUse`
and a real Turtle `skos:example` written against verified property names.

**Seven axes are now BELOW main on a corpus 335 terms larger:** scope-note, usage-advice,
annotation-coat, example, translation-coverage, competency-rationale, test-reach.

### Two count-only competency cells became exact rosters

`cqFrontierLabels` pinned `cqExpectRowCount 16` **with no roster**, contradicting its own file
header — *"a count-only pin would let the vocabulary drift silently."* It now pins all sixteen
frontier labels **by IRI**, including the three the rationale says a twelve-state reading
cannot host. Under the old pin, deleting a label would have failed on the count — but
**renaming or substituting one would have passed silently.** It now cannot. Proved load-bearing
by dropping one IRI and adding a bogus one and watching both cells red in opposite directions.

That is a *test strengthening whose side effect is the axis*, not an axis game: competency reach
is derived solely from the row cells, so the 26 terms gained are exactly the 26 IRIs now pinned.
The repo's other 34 count-only cells are all count-0 negative pins where a roster is not
expressible — left alone.

### Two things fixed beyond the ratchet

- **The branch had broken a HARD gate.** `axisTranslationCoverage` carries `floorValue 1.0`;
  main had **zero** untranslated localizable pairs in `logic:`, the branch had **113**. Now zero
  across `logic:` and `work-orchestration`. That was `slice-quality-gate` red, not a ratchet.
- An earlier branch commit had replaced the `sources` slice's import-provenance competency cell
  with a count-0 cell naming no term, **silently dropping three pre-existing terms' coverage**.
  The original cell is restored alongside the new one.

### Two axes remain above main — stated, not hidden

`fixture-pair` **+335** and `worked-instance` **+239**. Neither is a documentation axis: they
measure **corpus membership** — a term must appear as a node in a conformance fixture *and* a
counter-example, or in an example. Main is itself missing `fixture-pair` on **94.7%** of its own
terms. Sweeping 384 CURIEs into one fixture file to satisfy the counter is exactly the
axis-defeating boilerplate this work refused elsewhere, so it was not done.

`gmeow-docs` `lint_regression` green · `gmeow-slicetest` competency files all green ·
`example_sweep` 7, allowlist still 35.

## Stage 2 status — NOT ready for `/stage3`. `make check` is RED.

Leading with what is missing, per the rule that an unrun or failing gate is unfinished work.

### `make check` exit=2 — six failing tasks

| task | what I know |
|---|---|
| `check-lint` | `codespell` (**fixed**, `df92eb8b8`) + `markdownlint-cli2` exit 1 — **not yet diagnosed** |
| `rust-gate` | `docs_model_golden` insta snapshot assertion — a term-census golden that moved with the ~384 minted terms. Mechanical re-bless, **not yet done** |
| `compliance-report` | a conjecture-graph quad parity diff — **not yet diagnosed** |
| `i18n-lint` | **not yet diagnosed** |
| `slice-quality-gate` | **not yet diagnosed** |
| `wasm-parity` | **not yet diagnosed** (the GMN codebook digest drift was a separate failure and *is* fixed in `d02bf92d0`) |

Two exit-gate failures were found, diagnosed and genuinely fixed this pass:

- **`enactment-scada-control.ttl` violated the relational compensation law** — `compensatesEffect`
  bound to a `ReconciliationResult` rather than the receipt of the one committed effect. That is
  the law this branch authored working correctly on data that was always wrong. A `ReconciliationResult`
  names the class of effects a probe settled; compensating "whatever that probe found" is exactly the
  imprecision that lets a compensation be credited against an effect it never touched.
- **`GMN_CODEBOOK_DIGEST`** re-pinned to the embedded bytes.

`make regen` ran clean beforehand — `SHACL validation passed: no findings`, with only the generated
Python model projection drifting.

### What did land

17 of 21 planned gaps are closed, each committed separately with a production-surface
demonstration, and each posted here individually. The headline results:

- The **enactment gate compiles 42 kernel laws** and runs them on the real `verify()` path; it
  previously compiled none and could never fail.
- The **observed-not-derived safety guard** was enforced over an always-empty vector; it now guards
  the real reasoned closure.
- **All 16 frontier labels derive**; 5 did before.
- **RQ2/RQ3 means–end refinement runs on the native chase** with proof and typed rejection
  witnesses; it was a Rust BFS with none.
- **The conformance corpus derives instead of echoing** — 7 of 8 cases were byte-identical to their
  input, and the budget-cut case was blessing the inverse of its stated property.
- **The example sweep now validates against the module TBox**, cutting the `NON_CONFORMANT`
  allowlist **117 → 35** and exposing two real defects the allowlist had masked.
- **The OBI alignments are restored** through the sanctioned grounding route.
- Seven doc-coverage axes are now **below `main`** on a corpus 335 terms larger.

### Not recorded as a deficiency

Nothing was written to `.deficiencies`, and nothing should be. The six failing tasks are
**unfinished work on this branch**, not code deficiencies with a forward path, and the rule is
explicit that a gate that fails is work to finish rather than a ledger entry.

feat(1638): general prescription/enactment/commitment kernel and durable work orchestration

89 commits, 1463 files, +108351/−6939. Closes the durable-work epic: the
domain-neutral prescription–enactment–commitment kernel in logic:, its
work-orchestration domain binding, the native reasoning surface RQ1–RQ11,
competency cases CC1–CC6, the ten required negatives, and deliverables D1–D7 —
plus the gate-infrastructure overhaul the work forced, honestly labelled below.

THE KERNEL
- 44 authored logic: laws compile into violation rules and run on the real
  verify() path; 18 are relational (digest equality, chain linkage, lease
  overlap, retry licencing) after the presence-check bodies wearing relational
  names were split and given real formulas. Violation rules head on
  logic:violatedLaw so a record breaking two laws is condemned under both —
  the shared-failure-class head had let the chase keep one derivation per
  tuple and silently erase every law but one.
- The observed-not-derived safety guard runs over the real reasoned closure;
  it had been enforced over a provably-empty vector.
- All 16 frontier labels DERIVE from the lifecycle-axis tuple (5 did); the CLI
  prints the reasoner's label and flags a contradicting authored one as
  DISAGREEMENT, made literally true by a second audit materialization with
  asserted labels withheld.
- RQ2/RQ3 means–end refinement runs on the native chase as authored rules with
  proof and typed rejection witnesses from chase provenance; the Rust BFS
  side-channel and its third outcome fold are deleted. RQ4's pin DERIVES from
  an authorization proof (pins:1 on the shipped example, nothing hand-typed).
- §1's MUST-NOT (one good week never closes a maintenance goal) is an
  executing law with a red/green pair, not prose; required negative 10 is
  condemned by a law about the substitution itself.
- The conformance corpus derives instead of echoing: profiles name shipped
  rule IRIs and the harness hard-fails on an IRI the module no longer declares
  — renaming one rule reds 8 of 9 cases. The budget-cut golden records a real
  cut over a real frontier.
- RDF 1.2 statement metadata is lowered for the reasoner (Principle 17): a
  rule derives that a recommendation is CONTESTED when co-equal vantages
  oppose on one statement, live on the shipped example; the residue is a
  narrow logic:expressivenessBoundary (nested triple terms, term identity).
- Grounding: workflow correspondences (P-Plan, PROV-O, BPMN, OPMW, RO-Crate,
  engines, openEHR, schema.org) authored in the kernel per GROUNDING.md, with
  rewritten justifications (the old ones cited deleted vocabulary); OBI
  restored via the sanctioned route; 52 catalog families dogfooded as ontology
  individuals (the hardcoded test array is gone) with a production gate; the
  schema-org-procedures projection profile restored and a both-ways profile
  inventory gate added; the PROV-O/schema.org residue carve-out is a typed,
  ceiling-pinned record.

GATE INFRASTRUCTURE (forced by this work, in scope by owner direction)
- make regen removed as an entry point; check-sync is the single producer.
- Gate DAG on accurate dependencies; rust-gate split; heavy lanes (wasm-parity,
  acceptance, bench-soak) CI-only but still on every PR under quality.
- Three whole-corpus recomputations replaced by record reads with freshness
  guards that digest inputs AND the record itself (a {:.6} score projection
  that rounded a failing floor to a pass is fixed; DocMaturity no longer
  scores a vacuous 1.0 when the model cannot build).
- Host gate lock: override removed, moved off tmpfs, stale-owner reaping.
- CI OOM fixed by analysis: retention bounded to the live frontier
  (drop-after-last-consumer), and the two whole-dataset export leaves
  (export-export peaks 9.06 GiB) serialized on the dogfooded
  serializationBufferResource permit. /tmp littering ended: 72 leaked temp
  dirs to RAII plus a repo-static ban. docs/GATE-AND-PIPELINE.md records the
  twelve principles, each grounded in a defect fixed here.

GATES AND CONSTRAINTS
- .goals respected: greenfield (inferior paths deleted, not kept), Rust-only,
  RDF 1.2 first-class, data flows slices→gts, no silent degradation. No floor
  or ceiling lowered; every ratchet at or below main (fixture-pair finished 38
  BELOW main after full burn-down, chosen over rebaseline); NON_CONFORMANT
  allowlist 117→33 with the sweep now validating against module TBoxes.
- make check green locally: exit 0, 20/20 tasks, ~7800 tests.
- Completion-adversary: three full passes. Pass 1 and 2 findings (F1–F6,
  N1–N10) each closed by making the criterion execute, with demonstrations
  re-verified in pass 2; the pass-3 delta adjudication confirmed prior
  closures discharged. CI green is the remaining external witness and gates
  the merge itself.
- Deferral gate: diff scan hits are ontology prose about deferral as a domain
  concept or notes that a stub was REMOVED — evidenced, zero real deferrals.
  .deficiencies: zero entries; nothing was descoped and no sign-off exists
  because none was needed.

CONFLICTS RESOLVED
Two origin/main integrations (42 and 43 commits), every conflict individually:
kernel relocation vs main's rdfs→logic:subClassOf re-authoring, i18n unions
with zero duplicate msgctxt, derived goldens regenerated rather than
hand-merged, main's drained .deficiencies taken wholesale.

body:
> **Tracking epic.** This issue coordinates the slice-authoring-factory work; it carries no code of its own and closes only when every sub-issue below has closed. Per `AGENTS.md § 5` (Work Sizing), an epic that no single PR can close is decomposed into blocking/dependent sub-issues — this is decomposition, not deferral: every requirement below lives in exactly one tracked child.

## Problem

Per-slice annotation coats and translations collapse into gamed boilerplate when attempted as monolithic PRs — the evidence is the closed grounding/math full-uplift PR (#1498): 1,184-entry templated catalogs, boilerplate `useWhen`/`avoidWhen` coats, class-projected named-individual mappings. The honest surface remaining on math alone is ~691 uncoated terms and ~1,383 untranslated literals × fr/zh, and every slice in the repo carries the same obligation. Downstream slice authors face it with even less infrastructure: `principia` (10 tierCore slices, ~635 labels, 212 definitions) authors plain hand-edited Turtle with **zero local tooling**, consuming gmeow by path+commit pin.

The quality machinery (measured axes, integrity guards, raise-only floors) already prevents regression. What is missing is the machinery that makes **genuine authoring cheap**: self-contained work packets, an honest intermediate state for translations, and a gate that kills the next template family before mass authoring begins.

## The concept: the semantic packet, formalized

`docs/SLICE-UPGRADE.md` already defines the unit of curation as a **semantic packet**. This epic formalizes it as a typed, machine-readable authoring obligation — `gmeow:AuthoringPacket` — derived deterministically from measured axis findings, enriched with all the context an author needs, consumable by humans, agents, and (eventually) self-authoring systems, and verified by deterministic gates.

**Propose–verify neurosymbolic architecture:** the symbolic side (axes, gates, oracles) emits obligations and verifies candidates; the neural side (human/LLM) generates. Generation is untrusted; verification is trusted; a score can ONLY move via gate-passing content in canonical slice sources. This is the seam through which future self-authoring systems plug into the pipeline.

## Workstreams (tracking)

Seven completable sub-issues, each a single landable PR behind the ratcheted floor. Foundation A is split into a pure-refactor A1 and the new-surface A2 to isolate landing risk.

- [ ] **#1531 — A1** de-wire the slice-quality engine + make it wheel-shippable *(pure refactor; foundation)*
- [ ] **#1532 — A2** `gmeow slice quality/lint` consumer subcommands
- [ ] **#1533 — B** `gmeow:AuthoringPacket` type + brief projection + `gmeow slice brief`
- [ ] **#1534 — C** fuzzy-gated translation coverage
- [ ] **#1535 — D** distinctiveness / near-duplicate guard
- [ ] **#1536 — E** MCP surface: consumer `slice_quality`, `slice_brief`, candidate submission
- [ ] **#1537 — F** batch contract + fr/zh glossary lint

### Dependency DAG

```
A1 (#1531) ──▶ A2 (#1532) ──▶ B (#1533) ──▶ E (#1536)
     └──────────────────────────────────────▶ E (#1536)
C (#1534) ─┐
D (#1535) ─┼──▶ F (#1537)
B (#1533) ─┘
```

Edges: #1531 ▶ {#1532, #1536}; #1532 ▶ #1533; #1533 ▶ {#1536, #1537}; #1534 ▶ #1537; #1535 ▶ #1537. #1536 and #1537 are leaves. Buildable-now front: **#1531, #1534, #1535** (nothing blocks them).

### Two corrections verified against the code (folded into the children)

- **No path-escape guard exists** to lift (A1): `dev_slice_quality.rs` does no `canonicalize`/`starts_with(root)`/`..` rejection — arbitrary dirs are already accepted. The real blockers are the repo-path-wired rubric, the wheel-only razor, and the two repo-anchored axes (`gmn1_coverage`, `DocMaturity`).
- **`gmeow:TermEquivalence` carries no fr/zh labels** (B): its only label fields are optional *English* `subjectLabel`/`objectLabel`; translations live in per-slice `.po` catalogs. The brief must **join** TermEquivalence cells with the `.po` index, not pull fr/zh from the cells.

## Non-goals

- No LLM calls inside the deterministic pipeline (drafting happens out-of-pipeline via CLI/MCP consumers).
- No auto-derived floors (NO-CALIBRATION — the seeder stays emit-only, commitment stays a human decision).
- No coats authored by template.

## Decomposed into blocking/dependent sub-issues

This epic was an *uncompletable monolith* — six workstreams, `complexity-hard`, whose own risk log warned a one-PR attempt "repeats the #1498 monolith failure." Under the newly-codified **`AGENTS.md § 5 — Work Sizing: Decompose, Never Defer`** (PR #1538), it is now decomposed into seven completable sub-issues, each a single landable PR behind the ratcheted floor:

| Child | Workstream | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|
| #1531 A1 | de-wire engine + wheel-shippable (pure refactor) | — |
| #1532 A2 | `gmeow slice quality/lint` subcommands | #1531 |
| #1533 B  | `AuthoringPacket` + brief projection + `gmeow slice brief` | #1532 |
| #1534 C  | fuzzy-gated translation coverage | — |
| #1535 D  | distinctiveness / near-duplicate guard | — |
| #1536 E  | MCP surface (consumer `slice_quality`, `slice_brief`, submission) | #1531, #1533 |
| #1537 F  | batch contract + fr/zh glossary lint | #1533, #1534, #1535 |

Buildable-now front (nothing blocks them): **#1531, #1534, #1535**. This is decomposition, not deferral — every requirement of this epic lives in exactly one tracked child; nothing was dropped. The epic body carries the full DAG and closes only when all seven children close.

### Reflection

**What I'm least confident about, and why.** Whether A1 (#1531) is truly a *behavior-neutral* refactor. Making the two repo-anchored axes "honest off-repo" is easy for the off-repo case, but if A1 also sources `gmn1_coverage`'s `slices/grounding/lang/module.ttl` dictionary and `DocMaturity`'s `generated/catalog/constraint-catalog.nq` from the embedded bundle, the measured scores **on the repo itself** could shift — which would ripple into the raise-only floors and mean A1 is not purely neutral and needs its own floor re-anchoring. Whoever picks up A1 should measure the repo-mode scores before/after and confirm no floor moves.

**What you don't know but should.** The wheel-only razor (`gmeow-cli/Cargo.toml`: *"NEVER a repo-maintenance crate"*) is a hard design boundary, and A1 crosses it by promoting `gmeow-slice-quality` to shippable. That only holds if the **entire transitive dependency tree** of `gmeow-slice-quality` is wheel-safe (no repo-path assumptions, no dev-only crates). If it transitively pulls a dev-maintenance crate, A1 grows from "pure refactor" into a dependency-untangling job. Audit the slice-quality dep tree (`crate-check`) before committing to A1's framing — this is the one place the "pure refactor" label could be wrong.

## Folded in from the local `.deficiencies` ledger

Draining the local `.deficiencies` file into tracked work. One entry recorded against workstream E belongs to this epic:

**Packet-closure-as-KB composition shipped as a weaker mechanism.** The enhancement-audit item was that `submit_candidate` would reuse an `AuthoringPacket`'s depth-1 CBD + definitional closure as the candidate KB. That is not what shipped, and the reason is structural rather than a shortcut: the bundle's `graph/authoring-briefs` carries the **sparse packet index** (covered-term IRIs, grounding cells, margins), not the per-term axiom/neighbour closure — that closure lives only in the base graph or a repo checkout (`assemble_packet`). A bundle-served closure-as-KB is therefore not reconstructable checkout-free.

What shipped instead: `submit_candidate` records the target packet/slice as provenance (`gmeow:candidateForPacket` / `gmeow:candidateForSlice`) and requires the KB supplied explicitly; the covered-term IRIs the packet lists resolve to full content via `lookup_term` / `doc_card`.

**Forward path.** A repo-anchored `McpMode::Dev` tool could assemble the closure turtle from a checkout and feed it as the candidate KB, closing the loop for in-repo authoring without changing the shipped consumer surface. Worth noting that the standalone-console branch (`paudley/1211-standalone-console`) has since split the MCP surface into a consumer leaf plus a dedicated `mcp-dev` crate — which is exactly where such a tool would now live.

Related by-design boundary, recorded for the same reason: `slice_brief` serves the packet as canonical turtle plus a JSON reading of the bundle's sparse packet body. It does not reconstruct the full `AuthoringPacket` model's `render_text`, because the model's rich per-term fields (coat / axioms / neighbours / closure) are dropped in `to_turtle` and are not in the bundle graph. The rich content is reached per covered-term IRI via `lookup_term` / `doc_card`.

## Problem statement

The repo-wide removal of the Python surface deletes `test_agentic.py` and
`slices/extensions/music/tests/test_music_notation_projection.py`, which pinned the
**agentic-memory provenance** and **music notation-projection loss-accounting** invariants.
These have **no native Rust twin yet**. This issue tracks recreating that coverage natively.

## Coverage to recreate in Rust (native conformance)

- **Music projection loss-accounting completeness:** for every `NotationProjectionProfile`, the
  union of its representable set and its declared-loss set covers every `MusicalParameter`; there
  is no orphan `ProjectionLoss`; and there is exactly one profile per `NotationSystem`.
- **Agentic-memory provenance:** the tool-call / claim memory layer's provenance store keeps
  verbatim content below a size threshold (~5000 chars) and switches to a `blake3:` digest above it,
  with faithful readback. **Precondition:** this applies only once the memory layer is reimplemented
  natively; if that layer is not reimplemented, this coverage retires with the Python demo it was
  written against and should be explicitly dropped rather than ported.

## Consumer

The `make check` music + agentic gates — native Rust, no Python.

## Target location

`crates/validate/tests/` (music loss-accounting conformance over the music slice) and the native
memory layer's crate tests (agentic), if/when that layer exists in Rust.

# EPIC — Closed-world constraint canonicalization: blanket shape-purity seal, zero legacy

Canonicalize the entire closed-world constraint corpus so every SHACL/ShEx shape is a
projection of slice constraint axioms, land a **blanket** shape-purity seal, and delete the
whole hand-authored shape corpus + the structural `write_shex` export. Single source of truth.

Driven by `.goals`/`.baseline` (no deferrals, no compromises, no optionality, keep no legacy):
the gate is blanket, and a blanket gate is green only when the corpus is clean — so the migration
is executed to completion, not softened to a "detector".

## Foundation (landed on `paudley/1193-shape-subsumption-blanket-seal`)
- Subsumption engine (`≡`/`⊑` over the `ConstraintComponent` lattice).
- Equivalence oracle + comparison-only SHACL→IR reader + non-vacuous cross-check.
- Lift = the projector's Galois adjoint, certified against the real forward derive.
- Blanket declarative purity gate (proven over the live corpus; activates at the terminal increment).
- Typed `Shacl`/`Shex` lookaside sidecars into `gmeow.gts`.
- `conformance/validation/` projection-correctness category.
- `gmeow-dev shape-equivalence` — the per-increment verifier and the **live coverage ledger**
  (exits non-zero until every authored shape is grounded; this is the epic done-condition, no
  staleable committed snapshot).
- Proving slices `inference` + `inhabitation` grounded end-to-end (14 classes), oracle-verified.

## Remaining increments (per-slice; each: lift → author axioms in the owning slice → oracle `EQUIV` → delete legacy block)
~160 legacy shapes remain, by owning slice:
- `slices/extensions/music` (~33)
- `shapes/gmeow-shapes.ttl` — re-home ~78 to owning slices
- `slices/core/epistemics` (~8), `slices/core/ai` (~5)
- `shapes/mapping-dsl-shapes.ttl` (~12), `shapes/test-dsl-shapes.ttl`
- `slices/extensions/{model-serving,graphrag,agentic}`, `slices/core/{temporal,gts,standpoint,pipeline,notation,kernel,concepts,learning,diagnostics}`
- tail singletons

Run `gmeow-dev shape-equivalence --path <slice>` to see a slice's current verdicts.

## Residue-bearing classes (no faithful shape projection — carried in the canon, ledgered)
Some legacy shapes carry `sh:or` type-disjunction, value-keyed `sh:SPARQLTarget`, or nested
`sh:node` conditions the dataset-derive cannot reproduce (e.g. `AttackShape`, `SupportShape`,
`AbductionCommitmentShape`, `InhabitationTenureShape`). These are grounded either by extending the
derive or by authoring the condition as a full-FOL `logic:` constraint (projecting to the SHACL
constraint surface) — never deleted with their check dropped.

## Terminal increment
When the ledger reaches 0: wire the blanket gate active into `check_repo_static`; delete all
remaining hand-authored `**/shapes.ttl` + the structural `write_shex`/`dist/gmeow.shex`; repoint
consumers to the generated surface. This is where #1193 closes (`Closes #1193, #1194`) — its
headline gate reaches production with `make check` green.

GMEOW needs **two compressed forms, never conflated**, organized on **two orthogonal axes**:

```text
dialect axis (semantic):   GMN-0 normal form → GMN-1 token-compact → GMN-2 compaction
medium axis (physical):    GTS bytes | canonical N-Quads/Turtle | zstd-dict frames | JSON-LD …
```

1. **Machine compression (medium axis)** — GTS binary + per-corpus trained zstd dictionaries for storage, packets, cache, and transport. An invisible byte layer. **Never model-facing: do not train or prompt an LLM on compressed bytes** — it wastes model capacity learning compression noise.
2. **Model compression (dialect axis)** — **GMN, the GMEOW Model Notation**: a token-efficient, canonical, readable textual dialect that LLMs read and write for training, prompting, repair, and generation. Inspired by the schema-once/columnar tricks of TOON/JTON/ONTO, but GMEOW-native — generic compact notations do not know what must be abbreviated, preserved, typechecked, ring-filtered, or forbidden to leak.

The razor that keeps the two apart: **physical compression is lossless and identity-preserving — a zstd-compressed claim is the same claim. Cognitive compaction is a NEW claim about older claims.** GMN-2 lives on the dialect axis with an honest `lossy` ledger entry and provenance links; zstd lives on the medium axis and never changes semantics. A dialect is an abstraction level with its own preservation contract; a codec is a medium ("Canadian-English-written-on-paper" is not a dialect).

Symbology is **ontology-native**: if `⊑` is the symbol for a `logic:` term, that is asserted on the term itself in the DSL (via `lang:Denotation` from a Sign in the GMN Script), and the GMN toolchain **derives** its lexicon and grammar from the graph. The notation cannot drift from the semantics because both are minted at the same waist.

The end goal: GMN becomes a **lingua franca for LLMs speaking GMEOW** — compact prompts, stable training examples, constrained-decoding-friendly grammar, proof-grounded repair loops, and an ecosystem surface (primer card, conformance suite, MCP verifier, WASM validator) that lets models we do not control speak it reliably.

## Formal spine

- **GMN-0 = the RDF normal form** — the *existing* narrow-waist canonicalization (RDFC-1.0 canonical blank-node labeling + content-sorted term table in `gts_compose`, per `docs/gts-narrow-waist.md`). GMN-0 is a *name* for something that already exists; it is medium-independent (GTS and canonical N-Quads are correspondence-carrying **encodings** of it). It mints NO rival canonical object and is trivially mnemomorphic.
- **GMN-1 = the token-compact LLM surface** — sigil records, schema-once tabular batches, ontology-derived glyphs/aliases. Well-behaved with ledgered loss; its round-trip gate anchors against the GMN-0 **dataset**, not any file format.
- **GMN-2 = lossy cognitive compaction** — a reified new claim about older claims, provenance-linked, get-leg-only correspondence, honestly `lossy` in the ledger. Sources stay retrievable; compaction never overwrites.
- **Every dialect level and every inter-level/inter-version relation is a `logic:Correspondence`** (get/put legs) with a `logic:preservationKind` judgment (mnemomorphic / well-behaved / lossy — vocabulary verbatim) and a loss-ledger entry, riding the existing `lang:translationCorrespondence` rail (Principle 17 applied to our own notation).
- **GMN is specified, created, and projected THROUGH `lang:`**: GMN-1 is a `lang:SignSystem` (engineered notation; `Language ⊑ SignSystem` holds post-#1271); its glyph inventory is a `lang:Script`; its NFC/confusables/canonical-form norms are a `lang:Orthography`; glyph↔term bindings are `lang:Denotation`s; emission registers as a `LangProjectionTarget` in the PROJECTIONS registry (preservation **derived, not declared**); ingestion of LLM-emitted GMN is a RUNTIME lane.
- **Namespace ruling:** `gmn:` is NOT a top-level namespace. GMN terms live in the main `gmeow:` namespace with `gmn`-prefixed local names (`gmeow:gmnGlyph`, `gmeow:gmnCodepoints`, `gmeow:gmnFixity`).
- **Dialect versions are first-class ontology individuals** — each released version (e.g. GMN-1 v0.7) is a versioned `lang:SignSystem` with a frozen Script + Orthography + alias-table snapshot; the in-band `@gmn` header and packet envelope resolve to that node. Inter-version migration is a correspondence whose preservation judgment makes the semver promise checkable (mnemomorphic iff additive-only; the overclaim gate polices bumps). Greenfield preserved: only the CURRENT version is authored in the canonical core; prior versions persist as frozen generated artifacts + migration correspondences ("lossy compatibility lives only in generated projections").
- **Envelope contract on every compact artifact:** schema version, dictionary version, alias/glyph-table version, security ring, standpoint, provenance, losslessness flag, canonical blake3 hash. Compression never erases semantics.
- **The optimization target is a metric vector, never byte size alone:**

```text
bytes_on_disk · tokens_in_context · AST_validity_rate · roundtrip_loss ·
proof_success_rate · repair_success_rate · generation_latency
```

## Architecture

GMN as lang: individuals + a small graft module (the #1271 grafting pattern):

```text
gmeow:Gmn1SignSystem_v0_1   a lang:SignSystem      # versioned; frozen per release
gmeow:GmnScript_v0_1        a lang:Script          # the glyph inventory (codepoint-explicit)
gmeow:GmnOrthography_v0_1   a lang:Orthography     # NFC, confusables, canonical-form norms
<sign> lang:denotation …    # glyph ↔ ontology-term binding; gmeow:gmnGlyph is a DERIVED convenience
GMN-0→1, 1→2, vN→vN+1       # lang:translationCorrespondence carrying logic:Correspondence
gmeow:gmnFixity / precedence / sigil-role   # only what lang: lacks
```

Sigil grammar (sigils are record-initial ONLY — resolves μ-as-measure vs `@μ` collisions):

```text
claim @c · evidence @e · standpoint @s · process @p · proof @π
defeater @d · modal @m · math @μ · lang_ast @λ · logic @ℒ
```

Record and schema-once tabular batch forms:

```text
@c{id:c9, s:tulpa, p:affectToward, o:project_x, v:curious_guarded,
   q:.71, st:self/current, ev:[e12,e33], mod:affective}

@claims[id s p o v q st ev mod]
c1 tulpa affectToward project_x curious_guarded .71 self/current e12,e33 affective
c2 tulpa trustToward coworker_y moderate .62 self/current e44,e45 social
```

Model-facing loops (both directions, every step a named seam):

```text
retrieve → zstd decode → canonicalize (GMN-0) → privacy/ring filter → GMN-1 → token budget → LLM
LLM emits GMN-1 → Rust parse → glyph/alias expand → typecheck → prover → store canonical → zstd
```

Training corpus = paired examples (NL / packet / proof-failure / retrieved context → target GMN-1), **rejection-sampled by the Rust parser/prover verifier**: parses, roundtrips, typechecks, proof obligation generated, no forbidden ring leakage.

## Lingua-franca design levers

- **LL(1)-ish, prefix-stable, newline-delimited grammar** engineered for constrained decoding; GBNF/Lark/schema forms emitted as **generated projections of the graph** (grammar drift impossible by construction).
- **Key order mirrors generation order** (`s p o v q st ev` — decide-first fields first); fixed number policy (2-digit confidences, no scientific notation — digit tokenization is a minefield).
- **Token-cost matrix across real tokenizer vocabs** (o200k/cl100k/Llama/Qwen/Gemma) as a `maint-` lane artifact over vendored vocab data; the deterministic estimator remains the gate. An ASCII digraph beats a fragmenting Unicode glyph, full stop; prior-alignment only pays if the glyph is cheap.
- **Self-describing**: in-band header `@gmn v<schema> aliases:<table>`; a generated ~500-token **primer card** distributed via llms.txt + MCP.
- **In-dialect repair loop**: verifier failures return as GMN `@err` records; `@patch`/`@retract` delta sub-dialect over stable record IDs; MCP verifier tools (`gmn_validate` / `gmn_expand` / `gmn_explain`) so external LLMs join the loop without local tooling.
- **Determinism as a runtime feature**: byte-identical canonical serialization → prompt-cache hits, KV-prefix reuse, training-data dedup.
- **Stability**: semver'd, additive-only-within-major notation surface (alias tables absorb churn); public conformance suite (W3C-corpora precedent); WASM validator (purrdf-wasm lane); deterministic GMN↔controlled-NL verbalizer as a lang:translationCorrespondence (free bidirectional training pairs).

## Prior art (borrow the tricks, adopt nothing unchanged)

| Scheme | Use |
| --- | --- |
| TOON | token-efficient JSON-ish notation; repeated-record pattern |
| JTON / Zen Grid | "schema once, rows many" for batches |
| ONTO | columnar notation for LLM input; repeated-key elimination |
| Turtle / compacted JSON-LD | interop projections; not token-optimal |
| HDT / binary RDF | storage/indexing ideas; bad direct LLM surface |
| zstd dictionaries | transport/storage layer only; never model-facing |

Refs: KL3M domain tokenizers (arXiv:2503.17247); ONTO (arXiv:2604.17512); JTON (arXiv:2604.05865).

## What is preserved

- The narrow waist: GMN-0 IS the existing normal form; every GMN artifact and every `.zdict` is a projection of `gmeow.gts` (PIPELINE_SPINE doctrine).
- The correspondence calculus and `preservationKind` vocabulary, verbatim.
- The PROJECTIONS-registry disciplines: register-or-emit-nothing, preservation derived not declared.
- Greenfield: no compat shims in the canonical core; prior dialect versions are frozen generated artifacts.
- No optionality: deterministic estimator as gate; real-tokenizer matrix on a `maint-` lane; hard-fail named failure classes, never silent repair.

## Flagship acceptance scenarios (the depth bar)

1. **Round-trip:** GMN-1 parse∘expand over a bundle sample is semantically identical to the GMN-0 source dataset modulo its ledger entry — the gate is medium-independent.
2. **Token economy:** a claim batch in GMN-1 achieves a ledgered token reduction vs Turtle and JSON-LD under the deterministic estimator.
3. **Symbology coverage:** glyph coverage gate green over all three grounding layers with zero confusables/collisions.
4. **Transport:** per-corpus zstd dictionaries beat dictionary-less zstd on small-record corpora; envelope-declared `dict_id`; byte-identical decompression.
5. **In-dialect repair:** LLM-emitted malformed GMN-1 yields a named failure class returned as a GMN `@err` record — never silent repair.
6. **Compaction honesty:** a GMN-2 compaction is stored as a new provenance-linked claim; sources intact and retrievable.
7. **Primer-card teachability:** a fresh model given only the generated ~500-token primer achieves a gated AST-validity rate on held-out emission tasks.

## Subissues

Blocker chain: S1 blocks S2–S4 and S6; S2–S4 block S6's glyph-lexicon derivation; S5 is independent once S1's envelope contract lands.

- [ ] #1372 — S1: lang: GMN dialect specification IN lang: (SignSystem/Script/Orthography, gmeow:gmn* graft module, GMN-0/1/2 contract, versioning, gates)
- [ ] #1373 — S2: logic: glyph enrichment — operator symbology plane
- [ ] #1374 — S3: math: glyph enrichment — mathematical symbology plane
- [ ] #1375 — S4: lang: glyph enrichment — linguistic symbology plane
- [ ] #1376 — S5: gts/pipeline: machine-compression medium — per-corpus zstd dictionaries + packet envelope
- [ ] #1377 — S6: pipeline/rust: GMN-1 projection via the lang PROJECTIONS registry — graph-derived writer/parser, round-trip gate, token metrics, training-corpus emitter

## Ground rules

- Author in the DSL, not generated artifacts. Every hard rule maps to a gate + a named failure class.
- No optionality, no feature gates, no degraded fallbacks; missing required things are HARD FAILs.
- Deterministic, byte-stable outputs everywhere; the superset law holds over every new artifact.
- Rust-first; **no Python**.
- Design doc (EPIC source-of-truth): [`docs/design/1371-gmeow-dialects.md`](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/paudley/1371-gmeow-dialects/docs/design/1371-gmeow-dialects.md) on branch `paudley/1371-gmeow-dialects`. No implementation begins until child issues are approved.

title: EPIC: GMEOW dialects — GMN model notation (GMN-0/1/2) + ontology-native symbology + zstd-dictionary transport

body:
### Thesis

The pipeline is single-carrier (`docs/PIPELINE_SPINE.md`): every stage enriches one in-memory `PipelineBundle` fed from RDF sources. Therefore every failure, warning, suggestion, and informational event the build produces is **context-bound** — it is *about* some RDF source context (an authored file:line, a focus node, a named graph, a GTS wire coordinate) and *emitted by* some stage. And because every stage is a morphism (parse: bytes→graph; project: logic→OWL; reason: EDB→IDB), every such event is a **witness of that morphism's defect or partiality**. Today this one concept is fractured across:

- 9+ hand-written error enums (`PipelineError`, `BundleError`, `TranscodeError`, `DocsError`, `MaterializeError`, `ExplainError`, `DiagnosticsConfigError`, string-newtypes in logic-compile, PyO3-local enums);
- ~800 `Result<_, String>` signatures (logic ~228, pipeline ~166, logic-compile ~127, validate ~88, …) that flatten cause chains at every hop (~480 `map_err` in pipeline alone);
- a dozen bespoke accumulators (`LintReport{errors,warnings}`, bare `Vec<Finding>`, `CertificationVerdict`, `GateResult`, `Advisory`, …) each re-inventing severity buckets;
- `gmeow_diagnostics::Report` — the good model — fed by only **two** stages into `graph/diagnostics`;
- the projection loss ledger, carried separately from the diagnostics that are its siblings;
- ad-hoc `eprintln!`-style logging that never reaches the carrier at all.

This epic replaces all of that with **one substrate**: a single diagnostic value that is simultaneously (a) the error payload that propagates through `?`, (b) the finding that accumulates in the carrier, (c) the witness node a later pass can annotate or reason over, and (d) the log event. Severity is graded data; **fatality is a policy decision at the emission site, not a property of the kind** — the same parse defect is fatal at the DAG-load boundary (`Err(…)?`) and collectable during a corpus sweep (`ledger.push`). A subtle logic warning in a reasoning step never aborts; advice is attached by another pass afterwards. All of it rides the same substrate in the carrier and exits through the same projections (SARIF 2.1.0, JSON, HTML, text, `gmeow:` RDF).

### The formal spine (normative for the design)

1. **Witness structure.** A `Diag` is a node in a **derivation/provenance DAG**: its antecedents are other `Diag`s and/or cited quads. The anyhow-style linear context chain is the degenerate (single-parent) case of the same edge set. Reasoning-derived findings reuse `crates/logic/src/explain.rs` (world-scoped reifier indexing, cycle-guarded DFS, deterministic cited-IRI ordering) as the DAG engine — no second implementation.
2. **Grading lattice + one policy morphism.** `(severity × category × standpoint)` forms a bounded lattice; gate fatality is a single monotone up-set over it — ONE policy function `grade → {fatal, collected}`, not ~480 scattered `== Error` tests. "Advisory never gates" and "`PermittedEpistemicConflict` never gates" become theorems of the up-set, enforced in exactly one place. Default grades come from the existing registries (`crates/validate/src/codes.rs`, `gmeow:ruleSeverity` binding/advisory in `crates/pipeline/src/stages/rule_severity.rs`) — no new interner.
3. **Loss unification (Principle 17).** The projection loss ledger and the diagnostic ledger are the same structure: parse defects, projection losses (purrdf `RdfLoss`), and reasoning findings are all graded witnesses, sharing the preservation-judgment vocabulary (mnemomorphic / well-behaved / lossy). `ProjectionLoss` stops being a bolt-on category beside an independent ledger.
4. **Logic-grounded algebra (maximal dogfooding).** The Rust model stays canonical (the substrate must report on input too broken to parse — existing doctrine, `slices/core/diagnostics/docs.md`), but the *laws* — severity ordering, the fatality up-set, category→gating — are authored as `logic:` axioms in the diagnostics slice so the reasoner verifies the policy morphism. `FindingCategory` already mirrors `logic:FindingCategory`; this extends the mirror to the ordering and gating laws. Grounding (Principle 19): finding/suggestion prose grounds in `lang:` forms; the severity ordinal structure grounds in `math:`.
5. **Reasoner-derived meta-findings.** Because findings are content-addressed RDF nodes in a provenance DAG, root-cause clustering ("these 12 SHACL violations trace to one missing `owl:imports`") is a *derived* meta-finding produced by a logic rule — not per-accumulator aggregation code.

### What is preserved (the custom goodness — normative)

From `gmeow_diagnostics` (`crates/diagnostics/src/{model,render}.rs`), carried over verbatim, not reinvented:

- `Severity{Error,Warning,Note,Info}` with alias parsing, `sarif_level()`, sort rank; gate semantics = no Error findings; exit codes via `cli_core::exit_code`.
- `FindingCategory` — the 8-way KIND axis orthogonal to severity, mirroring `logic:FindingCategory`.
- `Location` — physical (`path,line,column`) + logical + GTS wire coords (`gts_term_id/quad_index/reifier_id/frame_index/segment_index`).
- `Rule` + the validate code registry + `gmeow:ruleSeverity` grading.
- `DiagnosticAttribution` (slice IRI + role) — S5 provenance.
- Content fingerprints (`gmeowFindingHash/v2`) and deterministic ordering.
- All five renderers, including GitHub code-scanning hygiene (repo-relative physicalLocation, synthetic fallback anchor, IRI→logicalLocation diversion) and the RDF projection into `https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/graph/diagnostics`.
- The **standpoint/deontic advice structure**: suggestions are not flat strings — `crates/validate/src/advisory.rs` already models advice as a perspectival claim from a `gmeow:Standpoint` with a deontic modality (`AdvisoryProjection{finding, claim}`). The substrate's advice slots fold `AdvisoryClaim` in; advice attached by a later pass MUST carry its vantage (P9).

### Architecture

#### A. The value type — `Diag` (one word, context-bound, a witness)

```rust
pub struct Diag(Box<DiagInner>);   // one machine word; Result<T, Diag> costs nothing over T
struct DiagInner {
    grade: Grade,                  // severity × category × standpoint (lattice point)
    code: Code,                    // interned, registry-checked stable code
    message: String,
    frames: Vec<Frame>,            // context frames (linear antecedent chain)
    antecedents: Vec<DiagRef>,     // DAG edges: findings/quads this witnesses from
    source: Option<BoxedSource>,   // live std::error::Error chain (in-process only, §B3)
    at: SourceContext,
    attributions: Vec<DiagnosticAttribution>,
    advice: Vec<AdvisoryClaim>,    // standpoint-bearing, append-only
    tags: Vec<String>,
}
pub struct SourceContext {
    location: Location,            // path:line:col + GTS coords (existing type)
    graph: Option<Iri>,            // named graph the event is about (absent = honest)
    focus: Option<Term>,           // focus node (absent = honest)
    stage: StageId,                // REQUIRED on the ledger path (see §B4)
}
```

**Representation (normative).** The ledger is a **hash-consed, append-only arena DAG**: `Vec<DiagNode>` arena + `HashMap<Fingerprint, DiagRef>` intern table; `DiagRef(NonZeroU32)` handles (`#[repr(transparent)]`, niche-optimized so `Option<DiagRef>` is free); DAG edges are `Box<[DiagRef]>` handle slices, never owned children. Consequences, by construction rather than by code:

- *Cloning a projection path* = copying a `Vec<DiagRef>` root set over the shared arena — O(roots), zero node copies. Multiple down-projection paths with different loss profiles mint new witness nodes whose antecedents point at the SAME shared upstream handles (persistent structural sharing; no `Clone` of nodes exists).
- *Dedup = content addressing = identity*: hash-consing on the fingerprint means inserting the same witness twice yields the same handle; the deterministic-dedup invariant is the representation, not a fold-time pass (same content-addressed-IR discipline as the logic crate; ordering from the explicit lexical sort key, never derived `Ord`).
- *Parallel stages*: no concurrent structure — each stage appends to its own ledger shard; the presenter merges shards in the total order (stage id + fingerprint). Determinism is scheduler-independent by construction.
- *No `Arc`*: the arena gives cheaper sharing than `Arc<DiagInner>` (u32 handles vs pointer+refcount), full cache locality, and trivially deterministic serialization (indices are a stable topological encoding).
- *Lifecycle*: the boxed `Diag` (Result path) and the arena `DiagNode` are two phases of one datum — a live `Diag` is **absorbed** (interned → `DiagRef`) when collected or cited as an antecedent. Construction paths are `#[cold]`/`#[inline(never)]` (anyhow lesson: keep the happy path hot).
- *Advanced-Rust levers specified*: bit-packed `Grade` lattice point (meet/join = AND/OR; the fatality up-set test = one mask compare), interned `Code(NonZeroU32)` into the registry, `Cow<'static, str>` context frames (static context never allocates), lazy format-args capture in `diag!` for filtered Info-grade events (the tracing lesson). Optional, implementer's call: branded invariant lifetimes on `DiagRef<'ledger>` (generativity pattern) to make cross-ledger handle confusion a compile error.
- *purrdf at the boundary, not the core*: `Term`/`Iri` for focus/graph, `RdfDiagnostic` ingestion, span-table blobs via the blob store, lowering to `RdfDataset` quads; the fingerprint scheme aligns with purrdf-core's content-id machinery so a finding's IRI and its blob-store identity are one scheme. The hot in-memory structure is NOT RDF quads — no triple-building on the `?` path.

thiserror's lesson: structural failure classes that today justify enum variants (`ResourceMismatch{stage,rdf,rust}`, `CacheMismatch`, …) become typed payload structs implementing a `DiagKind` trait (code + category + Display co-located; hand-written or via one `macro_rules!` — no proc-macro dep). `Diag::downcast_ref::<T>()` recovers them, so match-on-variant call sites keep working.

#### B. Propagation ergonomics (anyhow lessons, no anyhow) — with the sharp edges resolved

1. `pub type Result<T, E = Diag> = std::result::Result<T, E>;` — bare `?` everywhere via the blanket `From<E: Error + Send + Sync + 'static>`. **Coherence rule:** the blanket impl is the ONLY `From`; `RdfDiagnostic`, kinds, and reports enter via named constructors (`Diag::from_rdf`, `kind.into_diag()`). (anyhow compiles only because it makes the same choice.)
2. `ResultExt`: `.ctx("…")`, `.with_ctx(|| …)`, `.at(loc)`, `.for_focus(term)`, `.grade(Warning)` — replaces the ~480 pipeline `map_err(|e| format!("…: {e}"))` shapes. `bail!`/`ensure!`/`diag!` macros for emission. Display = outermost message; `{:#}` walks frames + source chain (and, for derivation-backed findings, the DAG via explain.rs).
3. **Serialization boundary (soundness):** the live `dyn Error` source chain exists in-process only. At the cache/carrier edge every `Diag` is **lowered**: the source chain becomes deterministic structured frames (code + rendered message), and ONLY the lowered form is content-addressed and pinned. Fresh and cache-replayed diagnostics are therefore byte-identical by construction.
4. **Fatality = call-site policy:** `return Err(diag)` short-circuits; `ledger.push(diag)` accumulates; promotion/demotion goes through the ONE policy morphism (§spine 2). A pre-carrier `Diag` (CLI arg/config errors) uses a distinct constructor without a `StageId` — modeled as a different entry point, not an `Option` that leaks optionality into the ledger path.

#### C. RDF source context from purrdf ≥0.3.1

- Parse failures: `purrdf::RdfDiagnostic{severity,code,message,detail,location,losses}` → `Diag::from_rdf`; `RdfLocation{path,line,column,gts_*}` is shape-compatible with `Location`; `losses` become `ProjectionLoss`-graded child witnesses (§spine 3).
- Parsed content: source-load stages parse authored `slices/` with `ParseOptions{track_source_spans: true}` → `SpanTable` (subject lexical key → line/col). Span tables attach to the carrier **as digest-pinned blobs keyed by authored graph** (reusing the blob store + pin-on-attach; they ride cache replay, no side-channel). Any later stage — SHACL, logic compile, reasoning, lints — joins a focus node back to its authored `file:line` when minting a `Diag`. This is what lets a *reasoning* warning point at the slice line that authored the offending axiom.
- **Span policy is a fixed rule, not a knob**: authored `slices/`/`dsl/` sources = spans ON, always; bulk `imports/` = spans OFF, always (their subjects are not human-fixable lines; honest absence, and .goals' "trim only at exit" is satisfied because no exit consumer of import spans exists). No per-call configuration surface. Memory discipline: span tables are dropped from the carrier after the last consuming stage (declared consumption, like any dataflow edge), with a test on the largest slice (25s-budget guard — the prose-lift corpus precedent).
- Non-span formats (RDF/XML, TriX, HexTuples) keep the synthetic-anchor discipline; absence is honest data, never guessed (epistemic-shape rule).
- Note: the span machinery shipped in purrdf 0.3.0; 0.3.1 is a formatting release. This epic pins ≥0.3.1.

#### C2. Maximal automatic capture — nothing load-bearing is hand-typed

The goal state for a rendered finding is fully self-describing: `source<line 12, quad 2, object position in file x> · locus<primary reasoning pass, stage-reason, level 4/9> · observation<found X, expected Y> · references<spec §, internal docs page>`. Each channel is captured **automatically**, at the layer that owns the fact — emission sites supply only the code and the observation:

- **Pipeline locus (ambient, zero per-site plumbing).** The scheduler already knows everything about *where* the build is; the ledger shard it hands each stage carries a `PipelineLocus{stage: StageId, impl_key, phase, level, position, pass}` (phase = the human name, e.g. "primary reasoning pass"; level/position = topological coordinates from the loaded DAG; pass = iteration for fixpoint stages). Every `diag!`/`ledger.push` stamps it implicitly — the tracing-span lesson: context is ambient, not threaded by hand. Because the DAG is dogfooded RDF, the locus links to the `gmeow:PipelineStage` individual — the finding's position in the build is itself ontology-grounded.
- **Emitting-code provenance for free.** `ResultExt`/`bail!`/`diag!` use `#[track_caller]`/`Location::caller()` so every witness records the Rust `file:line` that minted it (renderer-visible under `properties.gmeow.emitter`) — no macro user ever types it, and "which gate produced this?" is never archaeology.
- **Sub-statement source coordinates.** `Location` gains the statement-level channel the GTS coords already hint at: quad index within the source graph plus a `TermRole` (subject/predicate/object/graph — the "attribute") so a finding can say *quad 2, object position*. The SpanTable join fills line/col; the validate/reason engines fill quad+role (SHACL results already know the value/path; reasoning citations already carry reifiers). Absent channels stay honestly absent.
- **Structured observation (rustc's expected/found lesson).** `observed: Term|Literal` / `expected: Option<Term|Literal|ShapeRef>` are first-class typed slots beside `message`, not prose — so "suboptimal X, should be Y" is machine-actionable (diffable, remediation input for #1310, SARIF `message.arguments`), and message text stays out of fingerprints without losing the substance.
- **References resolve from the registry, never at call sites.** Each `Code` in the registry carries its reference set: external spec/help URIs (existing `help_uri`) plus internal anchors — the `gmeow:ValidationRule` individual, the generated docs page for the governing term, design-doc paths. Renderers join code → references at exit; emission sites cannot ship stale links because they never contain any. New codes without a registry entry are a HARD FAIL (invariant 3), so the reference channel is total.
- **"Fully reasoned-about" at exit.** The final render of any Error-grade finding includes: the derivation walk (explain.rs DAG → cited axioms/rules), the policy-morphism verdict trace (which lattice point, which up-set test made it gate), and the full locus chain. A finding the system cannot explain to that depth is itself an `IncompleteCheck`-category witness — the substrate reports on its own blind spots.

#### D. The carrier ledger — same substrate, in the spine

- `DiagLedger` becomes a first-class carrier member (peer of the blob store and provenance sidecar): append-only, stage-attributed, content-addressed.
- **Determinism under parallel scheduling:** ledger order is a TOTAL deterministic order — `sort_key` extended with `StageId` and the content fingerprint as tiebreakers; identical witnesses dedup by fingerprint. The byte-stable superset gate must hold under any nextest/scheduler interleaving.
- **Fingerprint discipline:** the v2 fingerprint and the `finding/{fingerprint}` IRIs key on `(code, category, source-context anchor, focus)` — NEVER message text or context frames (wording tweaks must not churn goldens or orphan attached advice; same rule that already keeps `FindingCategory` out of `sort_key`).
- Every stage may contribute; the presenter's fold generalizes from today's two-producer union to a keyed union over all stages' contributions, still emitted once into `graph/diagnostics` (transform-once razor), still a registered fanout member that round-trips through `gmeow.gts`. SARIF/RDF enrichment from spans lands with this phase.
- Pin-on-attach applies: a stage's ledger contribution is digest-pinned with its product, so cached stage replays replay their diagnostics (closing today's silent-drop gap).
- **Annotation by later passes:** advice passes attach standpoint-bearing `AdvisoryClaim`s / remediation / explain-skeleton quads that *reference* existing finding IRIs — append-only enrichment, ordinary RDF. #1310 rides here.

#### E. Logging subsumption

Events *about* the build's subject matter are `Note`/`Info` witnesses — into the ledger, hence into the bundle, queryable like everything else. Emission macro `diag!(ledger, Info, code, "…"; at = loc)`; console sink via `cli-core` `Reporter`/`ConsoleMode` (existing summarized/advisory text modes), replacing scattered `eprintln!`. Two honest carve-outs, drawn precisely:

- `transient` events (operational chatter: thread scheduling, progress ticks) render to console only. `transient` is a **closed, enumerated category** — not a per-call escape hatch. Boundary vs Principle 18: perf timings destined for the release-evidence lane are NOT transient — they are carried as data, as the Constitution already requires; only chatter with no downstream consumer is transient.
- The substrate works before a carrier exists (CLI/config errors) via the pre-carrier constructor (§B4).

Subsuming any remaining general-purpose (non-context-bound) logging is a child of this epic, sequenced last — context-bound events, the requirement, are core.

#### F. Boundaries

- **PyO3:** the documented exception contract holds (`MaterializeError::Parse`→`ValueError`, `Chase`→`RuntimeError`): kinds carry an exception-class hint; one shared `diag_to_pyerr` replaces per-crate routers. Reports keep crossing as data (`PyReport`).
- **CLI:** exit codes stay report-driven via `cli_core::exit_code`; `gmeow-dev feedback`'s fold surface becomes uniform since every gate returns the substrate's `Report`.
- **SARIF:** renderer contract unchanged, fed richer physical locations (spans) and the frame/DAG context in `properties.gmeow.context`; SARIF `fixes` unlock with #1310 (phase 5 of this epic).
- **Downstream consumers unlocked** (named children): LSP `publishDiagnostics` for live slice-authoring feedback (spans make it nearly free); `gmeow explain <finding-iri>` walking the derivation DAG via explain.rs; SPARQL competency queries + MCP agentic tools over the diagnostic graph ("all findings attributed to slice X", "everything tracing to this parse error").

### Hard invariants

1. Deterministic output everywhere: total ledger order (stage + fingerprint tiebreakers), content-addressed dedup, byte-stable RDF/`.nq` under any parallel interleaving.
2. The Rust model is canonical; RDF is a projection (must report on unparsable input).
3. No-optionality: unknown severity token, unregistered code, ledger attachment contradicting its pinned digest, or a carrier-path `Diag` without a `StageId` = HARD FAIL; missing spans/focus/graph are honest absence, never guessed.
4. Gate fatality is computed by the ONE policy morphism; advisory-tier and `PermittedEpistemicConflict` never gate — as theorems, tested once.
5. Source chains are never pre-flattened in-process; lowering to structured frames happens exactly once, at the cache/carrier serialization edge.
6. Fingerprints/IRIs never key on message text or context frames.
7. No new proc-macro or error-crate dependencies; cli-core's lone thiserror use is retired.
8. Typed domain report structs are **stateless views over the ledger** — they hold no independent findings store.
9. 25s per-test budget + nextest grouping respected; span tracking never on the bulk-import path; span-table memory bounded with declared drop points.
10. GitHub code-scanning SARIF constraints (physical location, repo-relative URIs, fingerprints) keep passing — the upload lane is load-bearing.

### Sequencing (dependency order)

0. **Base**: purrdf ≥0.3.1 / edition 2024 (#1330, parent #1314).
1. **Crate bootstrap**: `crates/errors` (`gmeow_errors`) absorbing `crates/diagnostics` (model + renderers move; `gmeow_native.diagnostics` import paths updated; no compat shim). Adds `Diag`, `Grade` lattice + policy morphism, `DiagKind`, `SourceContext`, `ResultExt`, `bail!`/`ensure!`/`diag!`, blanket `From` (+ coherence rule), downcast, `{:#}`, `Diag::from_rdf`, lowering (§B3), fingerprint discipline.
2. **Carrier ledger**: `DiagLedger` on the carrier; every-stage contribution; ambient `PipelineLocus` stamping via the scheduler-issued shard; presenter fold generalization + SARIF/RDF span enrichment; cached-replay diagnostics; span-table blobs at source-load with the fixed span policy + drop points.
3. **Pipeline adoption**: `PipelineError`/`BundleError`/`TranscodeError` variants become `DiagKind`s; ~480 pipeline `map_err` sites collapse onto `ResultExt`; stage `run` returns `gmeow_errors::Result`; goldens re-blessed where messages gain context (drift owned).
4. **Producer sweep + loss unification**: validate lints, logic verdict/ledger accumulators, scoreboard gates, advisories emit the substrate directly (domain reports become stateless views); the projection loss ledger merges into the witness structure (§spine 3); diagnostics-slice `logic:` axioms for the grading algebra + `lang:`/`math:` grounding.
5. **Annotation passes**: content-addressed advice attachment (standpoint-bearing `AdvisoryClaim`s); #1310 remediation + explain-skeleton enrichment; reasoner-derived root-cause meta-findings.
6. **Consumers + long tail**: LSP publishDiagnostics; `gmeow explain <finding>`; MCP/SPARQL surfaces; console sink replaces ad-hoc eprintln; per-crate `Result<_, String>` migration children (logic, logic-compile, validate, docs, conformance, music, CLIs); retire cli-core thiserror; general-purpose logging subsumption.

Child issues are filed per numbered item as work starts.

### Non-goals

- No behavioral change to gate outcomes: same errors fail, same advisories don't.
- No RDF-canonical diagnostics (doctrine unchanged — must report on unparsable input).
- No external error-handling dependencies.
- The conformance-harness verdict machinery is a separate engine and is not replaced here.

### Enhancements considered and declined

- **anyhow/thiserror as dependencies** — declined: neither can carry `SourceContext`/the carrier ledger; subsuming their ergonomics into a context-bound type is the SUBSUME+EXTEND+ENHANCE route, and the house convention (`crates/pipeline/src/error.rs:4-9`) already bans the deps.
- **RDF as the canonical diagnostic model** — declined: violates the report-on-unparsable-input doctrine; the vocabulary stays authored in the slice, instances stay projections.

### Related

#1310 (advice/remediation — rides phase 5) · #1330 / #1314 (purrdf 0.3.1 base) · `docs/PIPELINE_SPINE.md` (carrier doctrine) · `slices/core/diagnostics/docs.md` + `module.ttl` (canonical-model doctrine + vocabulary) · `crates/logic/src/explain.rs` (derivation-DAG engine) · `crates/validate/src/advisory.rs` (standpoint/deontic advice) · `crates/validate/src/codes.rs` + `crates/pipeline/src/stages/rule_severity.rs` (code/severity registries) · `crates/pipeline/src/error.rs` (house error convention this generalizes) · `docs/APPLIED_CATEGORY_THEORY/` (morphism-witness framing, Principle 17).
