# Implementation Plan for Issue #1336 — Diag substrate framework (Phase 1 + Phase 2)

## Context

Issue #1336 is a **normative umbrella META-EPIC**: its body is an authoritative
design spec, and it explicitly delegates construction to 7 sequenced child
phases (0–6) that together span ~1100 `map_err` sites across every crate. That
whole-program migration is *not* one PR.

**User scope decision (captured):** this session delivers a **top-notch, SOTA
error/diagnostics framework** — Phase 1 (the `crates/errors` / `gmeow_errors`
crate) **and** Phase 2 (the carrier-borne `DiagLedger`) — the concrete
structure that all downstream conversion work builds on. The conversion sweep
(Phases 3–6) is **filed as GitHub child issues** in this session, each carrying
its slice of the 10 hard invariants as its acceptance contract, cross-linked to
#1336. This delegation is an explicit, user-authorized scope boundary — not a
silent deferral (see Completeness Contract).

The problem this solves: today there are 9+ hand-written error enums, ~486
`Result<_, String>` signatures, ~1100 `map_err` sites, and two bespoke
diagnostic accumulators. The epic collapses every diagnostic-shaped concept
(errors, warnings, advice, log events, projection losses) into ONE
content-bound value type `Diag` that is simultaneously the `?`-propagated error
payload, the finding in the carrier ledger, a witness node in a provenance DAG,
and the log event. This PR builds that value type and its ledger — the
foundation — without doing the migration.

## Baseline (overridable defaults, from `.baseline`)
- Reference `CONSTITUTION.md` principles; `slices/core/logic/design` is CANONICAL for logic work.
- Gap analysis is adversarial, not sycophantic.
- **NO deferrals/followups in-code** — but decomposing an umbrella epic into child *issues* (process flow) belongs in GitHub, and is user-authorized here.
- **BANNED:** GitHub issue/PR numbers or process-flow refs in the ontology or repo docs ("Per #928…"). Clean up any seen.
- On bugs: you see it, you own it.

## Standing Constraints (inviolable, from `.goals`)
- **GREENFIELD, NO BACKWARDS-COMPAT** — `crates/diagnostics` is *deleted and moved*, no shim, no re-export crate.
- **RUST-FIRST, PYTHON-SURFACE** — the substrate is Rust-only. **No new Python** (no new py code/tests/fixtures). The existing `Finding`/`Report` pyclasses move verbatim; no `Diag`/`Grade`/`Ledger` pyclass is added.
- **LOW/NO OPTIONALITY, HARD FAIL** — unknown severity token, unregistered code, ledger attach without a `StageId`, or a pin-digest contradiction are HARD failures. No feature-gated fallbacks. Span policy is a fixed rule, never a knob.
- **SUBSUME/EXTEND/ENHANCE** — subsume anyhow/thiserror ergonomics by hand (no proc-macro/error-crate dep); reuse `explain.rs` as the ONE DAG engine (invariant 4 — no second impl).
- **MAXIMAL INFORMATION FLOW / ONTOLOGICAL USE / GROUNDING** — the grading lattice + policy morphism are authored as `logic:` axioms (reasoner-verified), grounded in `lang:` (prose) and `math:` (severity ordinal); data flows to `gmeow.gts` (ledger round-trips through `graph/diagnostics`).

## Completeness Contract

Every acceptance criterion **for the framework itself (Phases 1–2)** maps to a
numbered task below and is expressed as an executable check on the production
surface. The conversion sweep (Phases 3–6) is **not silently deferred** — it is
explicitly filed as child issues in **Task 10**, per the user's authorization
that "all the conversion work can be created as subissues." The framework is
built to completion so those children have a real foundation.

| Requirement / Acceptance Criterion (framework scope) | Task # |
|------------------------------------------------------|--------|
| `crates/errors` (`gmeow_errors`) crate exists; `crates/diagnostics` moved in & deleted, no shim; goldens byte-identical | 1 |
| `Grade` = BILATTICE: truth/severity ordering `⊑_t` × knowledge/information ordering `⊑_k` (Belnap), each bounded with join/meet | 2 |
| ONE monotone up-set policy morphism `gate(grade)→{fatal,collected}` over `⊑_t` | 2 |
| Advisory-tier + `PermittedEpistemicConflict` never gate — proven as exhaustive theorems | 2 |
| Hash-cons merge is order-independent (`⊑_t`-join of severity/standpoint); contradictory grades at one anchor detected as a Belnap glut, never silently overwritten | 2, 6 |
| Interned, registry-checked `Code` in an OPEN code/preservation space (Phase-4 loss-rungs fit without ripping a closed enum); HARD FAIL on unregistered code (T3) and on unknown severity token (T2) | 2, 3 |
| All four Invariant-3 HARD FAILs bound to executable checks: unregistered code, unknown severity token, carrier `Diag` sans `StageId`, ledger attach contradicting its pinned digest | 2, 3, 6, 8 |
| The `DiagLedger` carrier path is proven LOAD-BEARING (drift+verify findings interned into the ledger; `RunReport.findings` sourced from `ledger.project_report`; deleting the fold moves the shipped golden) — not a dark parallel path | 8 |
| `define_diag_kind!` macro binds code+grade+message and registers the code at definition (mechanical-conversion seam for children) | 3 |
| `Diag = Box<DiagInner>`, one machine word; `Result<T,Diag>` costs nothing over `T` | 4 |
| `pub type Result<T,E=Diag>`; ONE blanket `From<E:Error+Send+Sync>` (coherence rule; `Diag: !std::error::Error` asserted); `downcast_ref::<T>()`; `ResultExt`(.ctx/.with_ctx/.at/.for_focus/.grade) + `.or_collect`/`.collect_all` push-and-continue seam; multi-label secondary spans; `bail!`/`ensure!`/`diag!`; `Display`/`{:#}` | 4 |
| No new proc-macro / error-crate dep | 4 |
| `#[track_caller]` captures the `?`/emit call-site through the blanket `From`, not crate internals (tested) | 4 |
| Reuse `explain.rs` DFS CORE ONLY (generic `errors::dag`; `logic::explain` re-pointed, Explanation/cited-IRI assembly stays in logic — no second impl) | 5 |
| Ledger = hash-consed append-only arena DAG (`Vec<DiagNode>` + intern), `DiagRef(NonZeroU32)` niche + overflow HARD FAIL, edges `Box<[Fingerprint]>`, NO `Arc`, dedup=content-address=identity, attach cycle-guard | 6 |
| Source chains never pre-flattened in-process; lowered to structured frames exactly ONCE at cache/carrier edge; fresh ≡ cache-replayed byte-identical; `Diag: !Serialize`; no serialized artifact encodes an arena `DiagRef` | 6 |
| Fingerprints/IRIs key on `(code, category, source-context anchor, focus)` via length-prefixed/domain-separated hashing — never message/frames; `Slot` difference does not silently collapse (identity or multiset merge); public `DiagFingerprint→IRI` minting | 6 |
| `Diag::from_rdf`(RdfDiagnostic); `Location::from_rdf`(RdfLocation); purrdf losses → `ProjectionLoss`-graded child witnesses; double-lowering across two stages is idempotent (tested) | 7 |
| `DiagLedger` first-class carrier member; every-stage contribution; total deterministic order (StageId+fingerprint); pin-on-attach cached replay; HARD FAIL on carrier `Diag` sans StageId | 8 |
| Ambient `PipelineLocus` (scheduler shard) + `#[track_caller]` emitter file:line + sub-statement coords (quad idx + `TermRole`) | 8 |
| Presenter fold generalized from 2 producers → keyed union over all stages, emitted once into `graph/diagnostics`, round-trips through `gmeow.gts` | 8 |
| Span tables as digest-pinned blobs keyed by authored graph; FIXED policy (`slices/`+`dsl/` ON, `imports/` OFF); dropped after last consuming stage; consuming spans after the drop point is a HARD FAIL, never a spanless render | 8 |
| Deterministic output byte-stable under any parallel/nextest interleaving (incl. an explicit SARIF byte/ordering golden) | 8 |
| 25s per-test budget + nextest grouping respected; span tracking never on bulk-import path | 8 |
| GitHub code-scanning SARIF constraints keep passing (renderer contract unchanged) | 1, 8 |
| Grading policy REUSES the existing `logic:` Belnap axis + `logic:StandpointContextAxis` + `gmeow:Finding ⊑ gmeow:Observation` (NOT a fresh `gmeow:Grade ⊑ logic:QualityValue`); policy morphism authored as `logic:` axiom, `lang:`/`math:` grounding; two never-gate entailment theorems; reasoner-derived `gatesFatal` set EQUALS Rust `gate()==Fatal` set over the corpus | 9 |
| Conversion sweep (Phases 3–6) filed as cross-linked child issues (USER-AUTHORIZED delegation) | 10 |
| `make check` + `make regenerate` green; goldens re-blessed where messages gain context | 11 |

## Enhancements Considered and Declined

**Adopted from the Enhancement Audit** (folded into the tasks below): the
**bilattice `Grade`** (truth/severity ordering × knowledge/information ordering
— T1, fixes an order-dependent hash-cons grade-merge bug); **grounding in the
existing `logic:` Belnap + `logic:StandpointContextAxis` + `gmeow:Observation`
vocabulary instead of minting `gmeow:Grade ⊑ logic:QualityValue`** (T2, a #388
parallel-construct compliance fix that *shrinks* Task 9); an **open
registry-checked code/preservation space** so Phase 4 loss-unification isn't
blocked by a closed enum (T3); `define_diag_kind!` code+grade+message binding
macro (U1); `ResultExt::or_collect`/`collect_all` push-and-continue seam (U2);
multi-label secondary spans (U3); `DiagFingerprint→IRI` public minting (U4); an
`assert_diag_snapshot!` render-test helper (U5); DFS-core-only `explain.rs`
extraction (L1); reuse of the existing content-address / quantitative-axis
discipline (L2/L3); and robustness tests R1–R9 (Slot data-loss under hash-cons,
length-prefixed fingerprint hashing, `#[track_caller]`-through-`From`,
double-lowering, no-arena-index-in-bytes, span-liveness hard-fail, attach cycle
guard, SARIF byte golden, `NonZeroU32` overflow hard-fail).

**Declined (closed design decisions, not deferrals):**
- **Sheaf-of-witnesses over the graph site** (T4) — *Declined for this PR.* The
  `(graph, subject, span)` index genuinely forms a presheaf and a sheaf would
  let us glue local findings and detect gluing obstructions (true global
  inconsistency). But it is L-cost and no Phase 3–6 child needs gluing: the
  bilattice already delivers meet/join over evidence and Belnap conflict
  detection, which is the structure the children call. The lesser structure
  suffices because gating and root-cause are anchor-local lattice operations,
  not global sections; the presheaf shape is preserved (span-table-keyed-by-graph
  + subject-anchored fingerprints) so a future sheaf layer is additive, not a
  rebuild. Recorded as the theory the anchoring is a shadow of; build nothing.
- **Branded invariant lifetimes on `DiagRef<'ledger>` (generativity)** — the epic
  marks this "optional, implementer's call." *Declined:* the single-owner,
  single-`DiagLedger`-per-run design has no cross-ledger handles, so the runtime
  failure it prevents cannot occur; the `NonZeroU32` niche + content-addressed
  fingerprints already give identity. Lifetime plumbing on every `DiagRef`
  signature for zero reachable bug is not worth it.
- **Full graded-monad accumulation over `?`** — *Declined:* the ledger already
  accumulates witnesses explicitly at stage joins (and U2's `or_collect` covers
  the push path); making `?` itself grade-accumulating needs a custom `Try` impl
  (unstable). This is the *propagation* path; the bilattice structure lives in
  the *ledger join*, which we do build.

## Task 0: Worktree & Branch Setup (MANDATORY FIRST STEP)

1. Resolve top-level repo and set names:
   ```bash
   REPO_ROOT=$(git worktree list --porcelain | awk '/^worktree /{print $2; exit}')
   BRANCH="paudley/1336-errors-diag-substrate"
   WORKTREE="$REPO_ROOT/.worktrees/1336-errors-diag-substrate"
   ```
2. Keep `.worktrees/` out of git locally:
   ```bash
   EXCL="$REPO_ROOT/.git/info/exclude"
   grep -qxF '/.worktrees/' "$EXCL" 2>/dev/null || echo '/.worktrees/' >> "$EXCL"
   ```
3. Create the worktree on a fresh branch off up-to-date main, enter it:
   ```bash
   git -C "$REPO_ROOT" fetch origin
   git -C "$REPO_ROOT" worktree add "$WORKTREE" -b "$BRANCH" origin/main
   cd "$WORKTREE"
   git branch --show-current   # MUST show the feature branch, NOT main
   ```
4. Re-establish baseline (worktrees inherit no built artifacts): `uv sync`,
   `make native-py` (build native PyO3 exts BEFORE regenerate/validate — fresh
   worktree needs libpython RUSTFLAGS), then confirm green with
   `make check && make rust-test` before implementing.
5. Post this plan to the issue:
   ```bash
   gh issue comment 1336 --body-file /home/paudley/.claude/plans/1336-vast-barto.md
   ```

**⚠️ DO NOT proceed to Task 1 until the worktree exists, you are on the feature branch, and the baseline is green.**

## Task 1: Bootstrap `crates/errors` by moving `crates/diagnostics` (behavior-preserving)

Create `crates/errors` (`gmeow-errors` pkg, `gmeow_errors` lib). **Move**
`diagnostics/src/{model.rs,render.rs,py.rs,lib.rs}` and `snapshots/` verbatim
into `crates/errors/src`; **delete** `crates/diagnostics`. Add `purrdf` +
`blake3` deps (leaf: no `gmeow-*` deps). Re-point ~11 `Cargo.toml`s
(`gmeow-diagnostics` → `gmeow-errors`, incl. the two `/python` feature refs) and
workspace `members`; rename ~60 `use gmeow_diagnostics::` → `use gmeow_errors::`
across `validate`(25)/`pipeline`(12)/`gmeow-dev-cli`(8)/`logic`(7)/`docs`(4)/
`lsp`(2)/six single-site crates. The Rust crate/module fully renames to
`gmeow_errors`; **only the external Python import path `gmeow_native.diagnostics`
is held stable** — this is permitted projection-layer *consumer-surface* compat
(CONSTITUTION P4/P13), NOT a core shim (the core is greenfield-renamed). Also add
the `assert_diag_snapshot!` render-test helper (U5) so downstream children share
one diagnostic-render test surface. Verify no `#NNNN` process ref rides along in
any moved `.rs`/`.snap`.

**Executable acceptance:** `cargo build -p gmeow-errors` succeeds; the moved
`render.rs` insta snapshots + `gmeowFindingHash/v2` fingerprints are
**byte-unchanged** (`cargo insta test -p gmeow-errors` clean, no `.snap.new`);

  standpoint up-set); Advisory + PermittedEpistemicConflict never gate, proven exhaustively.
- Deterministic ledger: content-addressed hash-cons, order-independent merges (incl. the
  Stage-2 stage-attribution fix), byte-stable output under any fold order.
- Rust model canonical; RDF a projection; purpose-built ingestion boundary (`Diag::from_rdf`).
- No new proc-macro/error-crate deps; one DAG engine (invariant 4).
- MAXIMAL ontological grounding: the gate morphism is authored in `logic:` and reasoner-verified
  equal to Rust `gate()` — dogfooded, not Rust-only.

- GREENFIELD / no backwards-compat: `crates/diagnostics` deleted and moved, no re-export shim.
- RUST-FIRST / PYTHON-SURFACE: zero authored Python added (the only `.py` in the diff is the

  always-None `PipelineLocus.shard`.
- DATA FLOWS SLICES → gmeow.gts: grading vocab + gate rule authored in slices, re-minted into gmeow.gts.

## Completion-Adversary — STAGE=3 PRE-MERGE gate returned PASS (per-criterion demonstrations)

- [C1] Phase-1 crate — DEMONSTRATED: `cargo test -p gmeow-errors` = 81 passed; gate/lattice laws

  --test diagnostics_gate_morphism` = 1 passed; loads the AUTHORED rule (not re-typed), runs the
  native chase over all 96 grades, asserts reasoner-derived fatal set == `gate()` exactly + the
  two never-gate theorems.

  sequencing; children #1348-#1351 pre-exist; the headline substrate + ledger function without them
  (innocence test passes). Wiring the seam now would be dark code.

- PR body/comment hits are all epic phase-sequencing (Phases 3-6 = children #1348-#1351),

None. Integrating current `origin/main` (native-chase unification #1347 + put-honesty #1352) merged
cleanly (`ort`, no conflicts); `gmeow.gts` (merge=ours) was re-minted via `make regenerate` after

body:
Tracking meta-epic for the outward face of the projection doctrine: **every prior formalism is a lowering of one `logic:` IR**, on a lattice of four distinct relations. This is the completion of Principle 17 — the canonical statement is in [`LOGIC-META-SEMANTICS.md` § the outward face](slices/core/logic/design/LOGIC-META-SEMANTICS.md#the-outward-face-every-prior-formalism-placed-on-one-lattice).

## The lattice (four relations, deliberately not one "projects-to")

| Relation | Members | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `logic: ─isBuiltAtop→` | RDF 1.2 | ✅ substrate — never projected |
| `logic: ─isSupersetOf→` | OWL, RDFS, gUFO, UFO, **SKOS** | ◑ OWL/RDFS/gUFO lifted+projected today; SKOS is the gap |
| `logic: ─downProjectsLossilyTo→` | SHACL, ShEx | ⏳ #1197 |
| `logic: + mappings ─derives→` | SSSOM, EDOAL, FnO | ✅ built; being sourced from slice linkage in the correspondence epic |

## The shared foundation

Completing `adapter.rs`'s lift of the authored semantic surface into the IR feeds **all three** lower relations at once (restriction/cardinality lift → validation; SKOS lift → superset gap + alignment; one generalized purity gate). That is the blocker node.

## Children (sub-issues)

- [ ] #1199 — **foundation**: complete the adapter's semantic-surface lift (restrictions/cardinality) — *blocks the rest*
- [ ] #1200 — lift SKOS (annotations + `skos:*Match`); close the `isSupersetOf` gap
- [ ] #1201 — generalize the projection-purity gate to the whole surface
- [ ] #1197 — EPIC: SHACL/ShEx as the validation down-projection (V1–V4)
- [ ] #1202 — EPIC: derive `logic:Correspondence` from slice linkage; SSSOM/EDOAL/FnO fall out

## Related

- #1087 — Correspondence Calculus (the alignment leg's canonical object).
- #1195 — ADL2/OPT consumer, downstream of #1199 + #1197.

## Definition of done

RDF 1.2 is the only non-projected floor; OWL/RDFS/SKOS/gUFO are lifted-and-projected; SHACL/ShEx are derived validation surfaces; SSSOM/EDOAL/FnO are derived alignment surfaces; one purity gate forbids any hand-authored generated-surface construct; every edge carries a loss-ledger judgment; full `make check` green.

docs(logic): frame every prior formalism as a projection of one logic: IR

## Summary

Doctrine-only change that completes Principle 17 as a single explicit **projection
lattice**: every prior formalism is a lowering of one `logic:` IR, related to the canon
by one of four distinct verbs. Adds the SHACL Core + ShEx shape-surface design doc and
the canonical outward-lattice statement, with cross-references threaded through the
logic design set. No code, vocabulary, or generated artifacts touched.

## Files

- **ADDED** `slices/core/logic/design/LOGIC-VALIDATION.md` — the SHACL Core + ShEx
  **shape surface**, constraint peer of `LOGIC-SHACL-AF.md` (the computation surface).
  Closed-world data-shape validation authored once as `logic:` validation shapes
  (derived from the constraint axioms already in the slices, closed-world reading) and
  projected; emit-only; per-target loss ledger; the shape half of the purity gate.
- **MODIFIED** `slices/core/logic/design/LOGIC-META-SEMANTICS.md` — new section
  "The outward face: every prior formalism placed on one lattice": the four relations
  (`isBuiltAtop` RDF 1.2; `isSupersetOf` OWL/RDFS/SKOS/gUFO/UFO; `downProjectsLossilyTo`
  SHACL/ShEx; `derivesWith(mappings)` SSSOM/EDOAL/FnO), each grounded in the mechanism
  that realizes it, plus the three honest boundaries (substrate floor is not projectable;
  `isSupersetOf` is heterogeneous content-vs-expressivity; most of the superset relation
  is ExactPreservation — the win is single-source coherence, not new power).
- **MODIFIED** `slices/core/logic/design/LOGIC.md` — index row for the shape surface;
  End State now lists ShEx; a doctrine paragraph stating the four relations and linking
  the lattice.
- **MODIFIED** `slices/core/logic/design/LOGIC-IR.md` — the `validation shape` node kind
  now names SHACL Core + ShEx as its generated lowerings and points to LOGIC-VALIDATION.md.
  (The CLIF `logic:Module` paragraph from the recently landed CLIF work was preserved —
  see conflicts note.)
- **MODIFIED** `slices/core/logic/design/LOGIC-SHACL-AF.md` — points to LOGIC-VALIDATION.md
  as the constraint-surface peer of the computation surface.

## Requirements satisfied

Captures the architecture agreed across the design discussion: SHACL/ShEx as derived
validation projections; SSSOM/EDOAL/FnO as alignment derivations; OWL/RDFS/SKOS/gUFO/UFO
as lifted-and-projected supersets; RDF 1.2 as the non-projected substrate. This PR is the
canonical spec the implementation epics cite (meta-epic #1203 and children #1197, #1199,
#1200, #1201, #1202).

## .goals / .baseline constraints respected

- GREENFIELD, no backwards-compat: doctrine states the target directly; no shims.
- RUST-FIRST / no Python added.
- No optionality: the lattice is stated as hard relations with honest boundaries, not
  optional readings.
- No dev-process references in repo docs (verified: no issue/PR numbers in the committed
  design files; issue linkage lives in GitHub only).
- Maximal information flow / dogfooding: the relation graph is written so it can later be
  authored as real logic:/gmeow: relations.

## Conflicts resolved

- No merge conflicts on integrating origin/main (docs-only; re-merged, "Already up to date"
  on the final pass).
- During worktree consolidation the initial file copy from the earlier validation branch
  overwrote the CLIF `logic:Module` paragraph that had landed in LOGIC-IR.md on main; it was
  restored from HEAD and only the one-line validation-shape node-kind edit re-applied on top.

## CI note (honest)

All substantive gates green: rust (1/2/3), python, native-build, lint, quality,
ontology-generated/misc/reason/validate, wasm, capi, CodeQL, Analyze, external.mypy,
license/cla. The only non-passing check is CodeRabbit ("Review rate limit exceeded") — a
third-party AI-review bot rate limit, not a build/test failure — which is what left
mergeState UNSTABLE.

## Notes for future developers

The lattice exposes one shared foundation (#1199): completing `adapter.rs`'s lift of the
authored semantic surface into the IR (restrictions/cardinality + SKOS) feeds all three
lower relations at once. Build that once; validation, superset completeness, and alignment
derivation follow.

Upstream note (purrdf 0.4.2, 2026-07-10): `purrdf-entail` now ships a RIF-XML parser + materializer (`parse_rif_xml`, `materialize_rif`, rule sets with import resolution). RIF is therefore a candidate row in the outward lattice — `logic: ─downProjectsLossilyTo→ RIF` (and an ingestion lane) — with the ingestion half already built in our own dependency. Also a potential extra external oracle for the #1295 cross-check lanes (entailed SPARQL landed in the same release, strengthening answer-level parity checks per #1358/#1420). No issue filed yet; row to be picked up when someone takes it.

## Summary

Generalize the projection-purity gate from "SHACL-AF rules" to the **whole semantic-vocabulary surface**. Today `check_projection_compute_purity` (`crates/validate/src/repo_static.rs:308`) seals only `sh:rule`/`sh:SPARQLRule`. The outward lattice requires that *no* generated-formalism construct is a hand-authored second source of truth.

Design: [`LOGIC-META-SEMANTICS.md` § outward lattice](slices/core/logic/design/LOGIC-META-SEMANTICS.md).

## Scope

- One gate that reds on any authored construct in `slices/`/`shapes/`/`dsl/` that belongs to a **generated** surface (SHACL `NodeShape`/`PropertyShape`, ShEx, SSSOM/EDOAL/FnO artifacts, generated OWL profiles) unless it is either lifted-and-projected or carries a `logic:formalizes` back-reference — reusing the existing `formalizes_backed` legalizer.
- Subsumes the shape-half gate (V3, #1193) as one case of the general rule.

## Relationship

- V3 (#1193) builds the shape-half; this issue generalizes it to every surface once the lattice is in place. Land V3's shape-half first; fold it into the general gate here.

## Acceptance

- A hand-authored construct of any generated formalism without `logic:formalizes` reds the build.
- The rule-half and shape-half gates are unified into one check with no exemptions.

Tracking epic for making **SHACL Core and ShEx generated lossy projections of the `logic:` canon**, derived from the constraint axioms already authored in each slice — the shape-surface peer of the SHACL-AF computation surface. Applies Principles 17 / 4 / 12 to validation, exactly as the Correspondence Calculus (#1087) applies them to alignment.

Design doc: [`slices/grounding/logic/design/LOGIC-VALIDATION.md`](slices/grounding/logic/design/LOGIC-VALIDATION.md) (peer of `LOGIC-SHACL-AF.md`; cross-linked from `LOGIC.md` / `LOGIC-IR.md`).

## Status (triaged 2026-07-07)

V1 (#1191) and V2 (#1192) are **CLOSED** and their machinery is live: `ValidationShapeIr` is constructed (`crates/logic-compile/src/ir.rs` — `validation_shapes` / `with_validation_shapes`), and the derived-shape projection landed with byte/well-formedness/dogfood goldens for shacl-core/shex/shacl-af (#1401). The original "dead variant / never constructed" gap is closed.

## The remaining gap

- **21 hand-authored `slices/**/shapes.ttl` still exist** — the second source of truth Principle 4 forbids is still standing until V4 retires them behind equivalence proofs.
- The purity gate (`check_projection_shape_purity`, `crates/validate/src/repo_static.rs`) seals only the `sh:sparql` procedural fragment; the **declarative `NodeShape`/`PropertyShape` seal is explicitly deferred in-code** — V3's remit.
- **`conformance/validation/` does not exist** (only `conformance/logic/`) — the validation conformance category V3 promises is unbuilt.
- Structural ShEx (`write_shex` from the vocabulary FoldView) is not yet retired in favor of the derived lowering — V4.

## Children (dependency order)

- [x] #1191 — V1: derive `ValidationShapeIr` from existing slice constraint axioms (closed-world reading)
- [x] #1192 — V2: project the derived shape to SHACL Core + ShEx (one lowering, per-target loss ledger)
- [ ] #1193 — V3: shape-half purity gate (declarative seal) + carrier/gts wiring + `conformance/validation/` category — **in flight**
- [ ] #1194 — V4: equivalence-before-deletion — retire hand-authored `shapes.ttl` + structural ShEx

## Related

- **#1087** — Correspondence Calculus: sibling doctrine; a `logic:Correspondence`'s validation law (`π_target(d(g)) ⊨ shapes`) is discharged by a shape this epic projects.
- **#1195** — Full ADL2/OPT → `logic:`/SHACL constraint lowering (downstream **consumer**): an ADL constraint lowers to a `logic:` axiom → derived validation shape → SHACL via this machinery. Must not build a parallel constraint-derivation path.
- **#1201** — generalizing the purity gate to the whole semantic-vocabulary surface builds on V3's shape-half seal.

## Definition of done

- Zero hand-authored `sh:NodeShape` / `sh:PropertyShape` in `slices/` / `shapes/` / `dsl/`; the shape-half purity gate enforces it and the tree passes.
- Every `generated/shapes/*.ttl` and `gmeow.shex` is a provable projection of authored `logic:` constraint axioms; `check-generated` green; `gmeow.gts` carries them via the typed `Shacl` / `Shex` lookaside.
- SHACL and ShEx lower from the **same** derived node (cannot drift); each declares an honest preservation claim; the overclaim gate is green.
- Full `make check` green after integrating current `main`.

title: EPIC — SHACL/ShEx as projections of logic: (derived validation shapes)

body:
## Summary

Retire the second sources of truth: delete the hand-authored slice/root SHACL shapes and the structural ShEx export, once the `logic:`-projected surfaces (V2/V3) reproduce them. Greenfield, equivalence-before-deletion.

Design doc: [`slices/core/logic/design/LOGIC-VALIDATION.md`](slices/core/logic/design/LOGIC-VALIDATION.md). Depends on: **V3** (gate + wiring + conformance in place).

## Scope

- **Equivalence-before-deletion.** The 15 slice `shapes.ttl` + 3 root `shapes/*.ttl` are the golden oracle. The V2 projector must regenerate them **graph-isomorphically** before the hand-authored files are removed. Author the equivalent `logic:` validation shapes (via the V1 frontend), diff-prove parity, then delete the hand-authored Turtle.
- **Retire the structural ShEx.** Remove the vocabulary-`FoldView`-derived `write_shex` (`crates/pipeline/src/stages/export.rs:2273`) once the IR-fed ShEx projector (V2) reproduces `gmeow.shex`; keep byte/graph parity as the deletion gate.
- **Reconcile the two existing SHACL stages.** `crates/pipeline/src/stages/frame_shapes.rs` (from `gmeow:requiresFrame`) and `result_shapes.rs` (from `logic:ResultShape`) already emit `generated/shapes/*.ttl`. Fold them in as the validation-shape projector's first realized fragment rather than leaving a parallel emit path — or explicitly document why a given stage stays separate.

## Out of scope / longer arc (do NOT bundle here)

- Retiring the standalone `crates/shacl` engine to a conformance oracle by routing constraint **checking** onto the relational-core lowering. Note it in the design doc's runtime-relationship section; it is a separate track.

## Acceptance

- Zero hand-authored `sh:NodeShape` / `sh:PropertyShape` remain in `slices/`, `shapes/`, `dsl/` (the V3 purity gate now enforces this — this part makes the tree actually pass it).
- `gmeow.shex` and every `generated/shapes/*.ttl` are provably projections of authored `logic:` validation shapes; `check-generated` green.
- No parallel SHACL emit path: frame/result shapes are either folded into the projector or documented as intentional exceptions with a `logic:formalizes` back-reference.
- Full `make check` green after integrating current `main`.

---
**Series:** SHACL/ShEx validation-projection (V1–V4). Depends on #1193.

# Implementation Plan for Issue #1194 — V4: retire all hand-authored SHACL/ShEx; make validation a pure `logic:` projection

## Context

GMEOW's doctrine (Constitution P4/P12/P17, canonical design `slices/grounding/logic/design/LOGIC-VALIDATION.md`): the **only** authored validation form is `logic:`; SHACL and ShEx exist **solely** as ephemeral pipeline derivations of authored `logic:` nodes. Today the tree still violates this — ~440 hand-authored `sh:NodeShape` / ~937 `sh:property` blocks live across 21 `slices/**/shapes.ttl` + 9 `shapes/*.ttl`, and `crates/pipeline/src/stages/export.rs` still emits a **structural** `gmeow.shex` downcast from the vocabulary fold. These are second sources of truth: unreasoned, ungoverned by the loss ledger, free to drift.

V1–V3 built the machinery: the declarative validation-shape projector already derives SHACL+ShEx from the merged authored dataset (`crates/logic-compile/src/frontend.rs:1188` `derive_validation_shapes` → `crates/logic-compile/src/projections/shapes.rs`), the FOL-axiom procedural fragment already projects (`constraint_shapes.rs` → `generated/shapes/constraint-shapes.ttl`), and the V3 shape-purity gate (`check_projection_shape_purity`, `crates/validate/src/repo_static.rs:490`) seals the migrated FOL signatures. **V4 finishes the job**: reproduce every remaining hand-authored shape — declarative *and* procedural — as a projection of an authored `logic:` node, prove behavioral equivalence, delete the hand-authored Turtle and the structural ShEx, and tighten the gate so nothing SHACL/ShEx can ever be authored again.

Maintainer direction (this session, binding): full projection is the work — Hybrid "keep-in-place-with-back-reference" and "defer to a follow-up" are **inadmissible**. Every authored shape becomes a derivation; the authored tree holds `logic:` only.

**Transformational framing (the design this is built around).** The novel piece is a general `logic:Constraint → sh:SPARQLConstraint` lowering — the *validation* twin of the existing SHACL-AF *rule* lowering. It reuses the existing `constraint` IR node kind and the realized `logic:Formula` core (`∀/∃/∧/∨/¬/→/↔`, `logic:relation`/`logic:argument`); no new canonical construct is minted (the sole genuinely non-FOL family, aggregate-comparison, reuses the existing stratified-aggregation/`reduce` fragment SHACL-AF already lowers). This makes procedural constraints reasoned-over, content-addressed, standpoint-indexable, and loss-ledger-governed — exactly what a hand-authored `sh:sparql` block can never be.

## Issue Summary

Retire the second sources of truth under **equivalence-before-deletion**:
- Reproduce every hand-authored slice/root `shapes.ttl` (declarative + procedural) as a `logic:` projection under `generated/shapes/`, prove parity, then delete the hand-authored Turtle.
- Retire the structural ShEx (`write_shex`, `export.rs`) once the projected ShEx surface reproduces it.
- Fold the two existing SHACL stages (`frame_shapes.rs`, `result_shapes.rs`) into the projector / ledger; a genuinely un-foldable stage is a STOP-and-ask-the-user blocker (no self-granted exception — see Task 7).
- **Out of scope (issue's own longer arc):** retiring the standalone `crates/shacl` engine to a conformance oracle via the relational-core lowering — noted in the design doc's runtime-relationship section only.

## Baseline (overridable defaults, from `.baseline`)
- Reference `CONSTITUTION.md` principles (P4, P12, P17 central here). `slices/grounding/logic/design/*` is CANONICAL — `LOGIC-VALIDATION.md` governs this work.
- Adversarial gap analysis: assume the projector is incomplete until the parity gate proves otherwise.
- **No deferrals / follow-ups / future-work.** Work is now.
- **No GitHub issue/PR numbers or process-flow refs in the ontology or repo docs.** When repointing provenance (`metadata/references.ttl` `selectorLocator`s), point at the authored `logic:`/`module.ttl` source, never a process reference.
- On bugs: you own what you touch; fix it now.

## Standing Constraints (inviolable, from `.goals`)
- GREENFIELD, no backwards-compat, no shims. When replacing a shape, the hand-authored one is **removed** — lossy compat lives only in generated projections.
- RUST-FIRST, PYTHON-SURFACE. **Adding any Python is unauthorized.** Python here is only ever *reduced/redirected* (existing `validate.py`/`config.py`/`py.rs` shape-loading rewired to read projections), never added.
- LOW/NO OPTIONALITY, HARD FAILS. A shape that cannot project is a ledgered loss with the check preserved, never a silent drop or a degraded fallback.
- MAXIMAL INFORMATION FLOW / ONTOLOGICAL USE / DOGFOODING / GROUNDING. Validation is grounded in `logic:` and rides `gmeow.gts`.
- Data flows slices → `gmeow.gts` + `gmeow` CLI.

## Completeness Contract

Every acceptance criterion maps to a task and to an **executable production-surface check**. Nothing is deferred, stubbed, or left for a future PR. The issue's own "out of scope" longer arc (crates/shacl engine retirement) is recorded in the design doc per the issue's instruction, not silently omitted.

| Acceptance criterion (from issue) | Task(s) | Executable check on the production surface |
|---|---|---|
| Zero hand-authored `sh:NodeShape`/`sh:PropertyShape` in `slices/`, `shapes/`, `dsl/` | 5, 6, 9, 10 | Tightened `check_projection_shape_purity` green in `make check`; `live_repo_static_passes` asserts `rg 'sh:NodeShape\|sh:PropertyShape\|sh:sparql' slices shapes dsl` yields **nothing, period** (all deleted). The authored-tree gate reds **unconditionally** on any such construct — there is **no** `logic:formalizes` legalization in the authored tree (that hatch is the inadmissible keep-in-place, closed) |
| `gmeow.shex` + every `generated/shapes/*.ttl` provably projections; `check-generated` green | 2, 4, 7, 8, 12 | `make check-generated` green; parity harness Layer A (behavioral differential) green; `make validate-gts` green |
| No parallel SHACL emit path (frame/result folded into the projector; residue = STOP-and-ask) | 7 | Test asserting every `generated/shapes/*.ttl` block is emitted by the unified compiler funnel and carries `logic:formalizes`; `result_shapes.rs` (procedural) folded into the general procedural projector — no self-granted "documented exception" escape (see Task 7) |
| Structural ShEx retired; projected ShEx reproduces it | 8 | `write_shex` deleted; `export.rs` unit test updated; ShEx **set-differential** green: every structural shape encoding a real (authored-constraint-backed) obligation is reproduced by `validation-shapes.shex`; every structural-**only** shape being intentionally dropped is enumerated + registered as a ledgered ShEx loss (structural downcast ≠ contract, per `LOGIC-VALIDATION.md:116`); any real-constraint non-reproduction is a STOP-and-ask blocker |
| Full `make check` green after integrating current `main` | 13 | `make check` green on branch merged with `origin/main` (CI builds the merge result) |
| Loss ledger carries an honest per-target preservation judgment for every shape surface | 3, 11 | `procedural-constraint` = `ValidationOnly` registered via `target_meta`/`LossLedger`; `expected/projections/preservation-ledger.json` matches; overclaim hard-fails compile |
| Every migrated constraint has positive + negative witnesses (LOGIC-CONFORMANCE) | 5, 6 | Parity harness fails on any `logic:Constraint` lacking a ≥1-pass/≥1-fail fixture pair |

## Enhancements Considered and Declined
- **Fold `constraint_shapes.rs` (the 4 FOL-axiom families) into the new general procedural projector.** Declined for this PR: the 4 families already project correctly, are gate-sealed, and are a *special case* of the general path; folding them is a pure refactor with no acceptance-criterion payoff and would enlarge the byte-golden diff surface. Recorded as a clean design decision (the general path subsumes them), not a deferral of required work.
- **Retire the `crates/shacl` engine to a conformance oracle via relational-core lowering.** This is the issue's **own** declared longer arc / out-of-scope; recorded in the design doc's runtime-relationship section per the issue's explicit instruction. Not a silent decline.
- No other audit item declined — the plan is built around the maximal (transformational) design: validation as a pure `logic:` projection with a general constraint lowering.

## The method: parity-gated convergence (load-bearing)

The **parity harness (Task 3)** is the oracle that defines and gates all migration. It runs the *production* native SHACL engine over the conformance corpus and asserts the NEW (projected) union reproduces the OLD (hand-authored) union's findings exactly. Migration Tasks 5–6 are convergence loops: author `logic:` sources until the harness delta = ∅. Deletion (Task 8) is gated on delta = ∅ + green harness. **No shape is deleted until its check is provably reproduced.** If a construct genuinely cannot project (full-FOL/standpoint/world/time-indexed beyond the fragment), it is carried-and-flagged in the ledger and its check preserved via the canonical layer — never dropped, and its hand-authored shape stays only until the check is relocated (in-scope: all 30 files must reach zero, so any such residue is surfaced as a STOP-and-ask blocker, not silently kept).

Sequencing rule (from the design's risk analysis): infrastructure + harness land first and stay green with **both unions coexisting**; per-slice migration is guarded commit-by-commit; **deletion + seal-tightening + consumer rewiring land together** at the end (tightening the seal before deletion would red the still-authored files).

---

## Task 0: Worktree & Branch Setup (MANDATORY FIRST STEP)

1. Resolve repo root and set names:
   ```bash
   REPO_ROOT=$(git worktree list --porcelain | awk '/^worktree /{print $2; exit}')
   BRANCH="paudley/1194-validation-shape-projection"
   WORKTREE="$REPO_ROOT/.worktrees/1194-validation-shape-projection"
   ```
2. Keep `.worktrees/` locally excluded:
   ```bash
   EXCL="$REPO_ROOT/.git/info/exclude"
   grep -qxF '/.worktrees/' "$EXCL" 2>/dev/null || echo '/.worktrees/' >> "$EXCL"
   ```
3. Create the worktree off up-to-date main and enter it:
   ```bash
   git -C "$REPO_ROOT" fetch origin
   git -C "$REPO_ROOT" worktree add "$WORKTREE" -b "$BRANCH" origin/main
   cd "$WORKTREE"
   git branch --show-current   # MUST show paudley/1194-validation-shape-projection
   ```
4. Build the environment (fresh worktrees inherit no artifacts): `make install` then `make native-py` (native PyO3 extensions required before regenerate/validate). Do NOT gate on a full test run.
5. Post this plan to the issue:
   ```bash
   gh issue comment 1194 --body-file /home/paudley/.claude/plans/1194-buzzing-spindle.md
   ```

**⚠️ Do not proceed to Task 1 until the worktree exists and you are on the feature branch.**

---

## Task 1: Canonical procedural-constraint carrier — `ConstraintIr` + `LogicProgram.constraints` + frontend reader

Add the typed carrier so procedural constraints are authored in `logic:` and reasoned-over, reusing the existing `constraint` node kind and realized formula core — **no parallel shape DSL, no new canonical construct.**
- Add `ConstraintIr` (integrity `logic:Formula`, target derived from the outer `logic:forall` guard, `logic:severity`, droppable `logic:message` via `logic:loadBearing false`, closed-world reading via existing `logic:ClosureEntry`/`ClosedWorldClosure`) and a `constraints: Vec<ConstraintIr>` collection on `LogicProgram` (`crates/logic-compile/src/ir.rs` ~2325–2355), content-addressed like the sibling IR nodes.
- Frontend reader in `crates/logic-compile/src/frontend.rs`: read authored `logic:Constraint` nodes (and the pattern-keyed *sugar* records — mutual-exclusion, required-companion, etc. — that the compiler expands into the canonical formula, mirroring how `PropertyCharacteristicAssertion` expands today). Sugar is frontend-only; one canonical form.
- Unit tests: each of the 7 patterns round-trips authored → `ConstraintIr` → formula, with content-key stability.

### After Task 1: github-commit-agent → github-push-agent → post update to #1194.

## Task 2: Procedural-constraint projector + loss-ledger registration → `generated/shapes/procedural-constraints.ttl`

- `project_procedural_constraint(&ConstraintIr) -> String` in `crates/logic-compile/src/projections/shapes.rs`, driven from `compile_program` (`crates/logic-compile/src/projections/mod.rs`), emitting a deterministic IRI-sorted, blank-node-free document `generated/shapes/procedural-constraints.ttl`. Each block: `sh:NodeShape ; logic:formalizes <gmeow-term> ; sh:targetClass|targetSubjectsOf|SPARQLTarget … ; sh:sparql [ a sh:SPARQLConstraint ; sh:severity … ; sh:message … ; sh:select """…""" ]`. Lowering = NNF → BGP/`FILTER NOT EXISTS` negation-witness (the validation twin of the SHACL-AF rule lowering); P6 aggregate reuses the `reduce`/GROUP-BY sub-`SELECT` path.
- Ledger: add `"procedural-constraint"` to `LEDGER_TARGETS` and a `target_meta` arm = `ValidationOnly` (mod.rs:503/769); register drops via `loss.record_projection_drops` for any constraint exceeding the range-restricted/aggregation fragment; add the blanket `logic:unsupported` ShEx drop (SPARQL constraints have no ShEx form). `assert_no_overclaim` must hold.
- Wire `generated/shapes/procedural-constraints.ttl` into the generator registry / `check-generated` coverage (`crates/pipeline/src/generator_registry.rs`) so its bytes are drift-gated, and into the carrier fold + `gmeow.gts` members (`gts_sink.rs`).
- Tests: golden projection of a fixture constraint per pattern; a native-engine round-trip (mirror `constraint_shapes.rs:407`) asserting planted violations flag and clean data passes; confirm the engine executes GROUP-BY sub-`SELECT` in a **constraint** context (P6 — else P6 becomes ledgered residue, flagged as a blocker if any real P6 constraint exists).

### After Task 2: github-commit-agent → github-push-agent → wiring-verifier → post update to #1194.

## Task 3: Parity / equivalence-before-deletion harness (the deletion gate)

New Rust integration test `crates/validate/tests/shape_projection_parity.rs`, runnable green while both unions coexist:
- **Layer A (decisive, behavioral).** Run the production engine (`purrdf::shapes::engine::validate_dataset` via `crates/validate/src/store.rs:36`) over the conformance corpus (`tests/fixtures/shapes/*.ttl` + slice `tests/{counter-examples,example-conformance}/*.ttl`) under OLD union (authored `shapes/*.ttl` minus EXCLUDED + `slices/**/shapes.ttl`) vs NEW union (authored set with migrated blocks removed, replaced by `generated/shapes/{validation,constraint,procedural}-*.ttl`). Assert **identical violation sets**, keyed on `(focus_node, severity, formalizes-resolved-source)` — resolve through `logic:formalizes` (not shape IRI) so the rename is transparent; `sh:message` advisory. Both directions: every OLD violation still fires (authored ⊆ projected) AND NEW adds no violation on wellformed fixtures (no over-claim).
- **Layer B (coverage backstop, required-but-advisory on body-mismatch).** Reduce both unions to constraint-atoms — declarative `(target, path, component)` tuples (reusing the `ConstraintComponent` vocabulary + `format_bound` normalization) and procedural `(target, normalized sh:select body)` (absolute IRIs, whitespace-stripped, vars alpha-normalized, commutative `UNION`/conjuncts sorted). Assert authored-atoms ⊆ projected-atoms; a procedural body mismatch demands a witness fixture rather than hard-failing (SPARQL equivalence is undecidable — Layer A is decisive).
- **Witness requirement.** Fail on any migrated `logic:Constraint` lacking ≥1 pass + ≥1 fail fixture.
- Wire into the required-CI-jobs set so deletion cannot land without it.

### After Task 3: github-commit-agent → github-push-agent → post update to #1194.

## Task 4: Extend declarative derive coverage for systematic gaps

Close the derive families that Explorer analysis flagged as underived from authored OWL/RDFS (so the declarative migration in Task 5 has a derivation path): numeric/datetime ranges, `sh:languageIn`, non-`oneOf` `sh:in` value sets, `sh:minLength`/`maxLength` beyond faceted datatypes, and `sh:severity`/`sh:message` carry-through — extend `derive_validation_shapes` families in `crates/logic-compile/src/frontend.rs` (+ emitter already supports every family per `projections/shapes.rs`). Guard each extension with the golden projection test and the parity harness.

### After Task 4: github-commit-agent → github-push-agent → wiring-verifier → post update to #1194.

## Task 5: Migrate the declarative fragment to `logic:` (converge declarative delta → ∅)

For every hand-authored **declarative** shape across the 21 slice + (declarative subset of the) 9 root files: author the backing OWL/RDFS axiom (cardinality, `sh:class`↔range, datatype, nodeKind, value-set, disjointness, functional/hasKey) + the closure opt-in (`ClosedWorldClosure` for domain/range-derived range shapes like kernel's `useForConsumer`/`avoidForConsumer`; `OpenWorldClosure` opt-out where a shape must NOT derive) in the **owning slice's `module.ttl`**, so `derive_validation_shapes` reproduces the constraint into `generated/shapes/validation-shapes.ttl`. Iterate slice-by-slice against the parity harness until the declarative delta = ∅. Author witness fixtures where the corpus lacks a pass/fail pair.

### After Task 5: github-commit-agent → github-push-agent → wiring-verifier → post update to #1194 (this task may span multiple commits; each keeps the harness green or greener).

## Task 6: Migrate the procedural fragment to `logic:` (converge procedural delta → ∅)

Author every bespoke `sh:sparql` procedural constraint (the 7 patterns across `shapes/{statement,test,mapping}-dsl-shapes.ttl`, `shapes/gmeow-shapes.ttl`, and slice `shapes.ttl`) as a `logic:Constraint` (Task 1 form) in the **owning slice**, so Task 2's projector emits it into `generated/shapes/procedural-constraints.ttl` carrying `logic:formalizes`. Cover P1–P7; P6 via the aggregation fragment. Iterate against the parity harness (Layer A behavioral equivalence + witness pairs) until the procedural delta = ∅. Any construct that provably cannot project → ledgered `procedural-constraint` residue with the check preserved in the canon; if that would leave a hand-authored shape undeletable, **STOP and surface it to the user** (do not silently keep it).

### After Task 6: github-commit-agent → github-push-agent → wiring-verifier → post update to #1194 (may span multiple commits).

## Task 7: Reconcile `frame_shapes.rs` + `result_shapes.rs` into the unified projector (no parallel emit path)

Folding is **mandatory** — the maintainer direction (full projection) forbids a self-granted "documented exception" that leaves a live parallel emit path.
- `frame_shapes.rs` constructs `ValidationShapeIr` directly — route it through the compiler funnel (Task 2's `compile_program`) so its output is ledgered and carries `logic:formalizes`.
- `result_shapes.rs` is procedural (`sh:sparql` over the value-keyed reified-row model) — fold into the general procedural projector (Task 2).
- If, and only if, a stage is genuinely un-foldable for a **structural** reason (a distinct input model that cannot pass through the funnel — *not* implementation effort), that is a **STOP-and-ask-the-user blocker**: surface it, do not paper it over with a documented exception. The user decides whether a documented `generated/`-tree exception carrying `logic:formalizes` is acceptable.
- Executable outcome: a test asserts every `generated/shapes/*.ttl` block is emitted by the unified funnel and carries `logic:formalizes`.

### After Task 7: github-commit-agent → github-push-agent → wiring-verifier → post update to #1194.

## Task 8: Retire the structural ShEx

Extend the parity harness with a **ShEx set-differential** (not an elastic "coverage" predicate): emit both surfaces and partition the structural `gmeow.shex` shapes into (a) shapes encoding a real obligation backed by an authored `logic:` constraint — each MUST be reproduced by `generated/shapes/validation-shapes.shex`, and (b) structural-**only** shapes (bare domain/range downcast of unconstrained terms — never a real contract, per `LOGIC-VALIDATION.md:116`) — each MUST be enumerated and registered as an intentional ledgered ShEx loss. Any shape in partition (a) that is not reproduced is a **STOP-and-ask-the-user blocker** (author the missing `logic:` node, or get an explicit decision) — never resolved by loosening the predicate.

Only once the differential is green: delete `write_shex` (`crates/pipeline/src/stages/export.rs:2316`, emit at `:2535`) and fix the in-file unit test (`export.rs:2650-2705` — drop the `gmeow.shex` expected-member/`PREFIX gmeow:` assertions). `dist/gmeow.shex` is no longer produced structurally; the committed projected `.shex` is the surface. Note: the issue's `generated/dist/gmeow.shex` path is stale — the committed ShEx is `generated/shapes/validation-shapes.shex`; `shex_wellformed.rs:45` already skips-if-absent so tolerates removal.

### After Task 8: github-commit-agent → github-push-agent → wiring-verifier → post update to #1194.

## Task 9: Delete all hand-authored shapes + tighten the purity gate + update the constitution node (land together)

Only after the parity harness proves NEW-union ≡ OLD-union with delta = ∅:
- Delete all 21 `slices/**/shapes.ttl` + 9 `shapes/*.ttl` (data shapes AND the 4 DSL/manifest lints).
- Tighten `check_projection_shape_purity` (`crates/validate/src/repo_static.rs:490`) from FOL-signature matching to an **unconditional** seal: **any** subject in `shapes/`/`slices/`/`dsl/` typed `sh:NodeShape`/`sh:PropertyShape`, or bearing declarative constraint predicates (`sh:property`/`sh:path`/`sh:targetClass`/`sh:targetSubjectsOf`/`sh:targetObjectsOf`), or carrying `sh:sparql`, reds the build **— with NO `logic:formalizes` legalization in the authored tree.** The `formalizes_backed` hatch is *removed from the authored-tree scope entirely*: `logic:formalizes` legalization is meaningful only for `generated/**` artifacts, which this gate does not scan. Reusing it here would rebuild the inadmissible keep-in-place escape (a hardest-to-project shape left in `slices/` with one `logic:formalizes` triple would pass) — so it is deleted, not reused, for authored-tree detection.
- Rewrite the gate test `shape_purity_flags_unbacked_migrated_axioms_and_passes_backed_and_closed_world` (`repo_static.rs:1874`): its old "backed `sh:select` passes" and "retained closed-world `FILTER NOT EXISTS` passes" cases are now **inverted** — any authored-tree `sh:sparql`/declarative shape reds regardless of a back-reference. Add declarative `sh:NodeShape`/`sh:PropertyShape` red cases. Keep `live_repo_static_passes` green (trivially — the authored tree is now shape-free after deletion above).
- Update `governance/constitution.ttl` `meta:gate-projection-shape-purity` (lines 504–512) artifacts/symbols in lock-step (add the new projector symbol; `check_references` seals that every `meta:symbol` is a real Rust item in a cited artifact).

### After Task 9: github-commit-agent → github-push-agent → wiring-verifier → post update to #1194.

## Task 10: Rewire consumers (the shape union auto-narrows; direct consumers do not)

- **Validation union** narrows automatically: `purrdf-shapes` `shape_files` unions `shapes/*` + `generated/shapes/*` + `slices/**/shapes.ttl`; deletion leaves only `generated/shapes/*` (fail-closes on empty `generated/shapes/`). **No `purrdf-shapes` bump needed.**

## Binding architecture correction — equivalence before deletion is logic-to-projection

The migration recipe in older comments is superseded where it says to author backing OWL/RDFS axioms. Both declarative and procedural validation semantics must move into realized logic-native validation/constraint nodes and formulas in the owning slice.

Legacy SHACL/OWL/RDFS may be read to prove equivalence before deletion, but no new OWL/RDFS/gUFO semantic source may be minted during the migration. The forward oracle should compare the generated validation projection from `logic:` against the legacy surface. External-formalism outputs remain generated and loss-ledgered.

Required RDFS labels and ownership annotations are metadata, not an exception for semantic authoring. Principles 4, 17, and 19 apply.

## Counts have moved — real progress, and the numbers in this issue are now wrong

Re-verified against `main` @ c2b03aba6.

**This issue says:** "The 15 slice `shapes.ttl` + 3 root `shapes/*.ttl` are the golden oracle."

**Actual:**

| | issue says | actual on `main` |
|---|---|---|
| slice `shapes.ttl` | 15 | **10** |
| root `shapes/*.ttl` | 3 | **9** |

The slice count is genuinely burning down, and there is a ratchet enforcing it. `PINNED_HAND_AUTHORED_SHAPES_TTL` (`crates/validate/src/repo_static.rs:683`) pins **19** paths, `check_hand_authored_shapes_ratchet` reds on any slice `shapes.ttl` outside that pin, and the live census is 10 — so **9 have already been retired** and the set can only shrink. That is the equivalence-before-deletion arc working as designed.

The root `shapes/*.ttl` count going 3 → 9 is worth a look: either the issue's original count was wrong, or root shapes grew while slice shapes shrank. The ratchet covers `slices/<group>/<slice>/shapes.ttl` only, so the root directory is not under the same shrink-only guard.
